business_glossary_term: Terminal Elimination Rate Constant (Lambda-z) Estimation Method

description: Minimum number of data points required in the terminal phase for Lambda-z estimation to be considered valid. Typically set to 3 per regulatory guidance. Specifications below this threshold result in flagged or excluded Lambda-z estimates.

business_glossary_term: Lower Limit of Quantification (LLOQ) Handling Method

description: Rule applied when scheduled PK concentration timepoints are missing. Defines whether the subject is excluded from analysis, the timepoint is excluded, or imputation is applied. Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF) imputation is used in specific contexts per the SAP.

description: Specifies the trapezoidal integration rule applied during Non-Compartmental Analysis (NCA) for area-under-the-curve (AUC) estimation. Linear-up/log-down is the most common default in Phoenix WinNonlin for oral dosing studies.

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this SDTM mapping rule is defined. Enables study-scoped filtering and traceability of all mapping specifications back to the originating protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

description: Date and time when this mapping rule was formally approved and promoted to 'approved' status by the authorized reviewer. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this mapping lifecycle transition. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature audit trail.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Free-text justification for the most recent change to this mapping rule (e.g., 'Protocol Amendment 3 — new AE severity scale', 'Corrected derivation logic per QC review'). Required when mapping_status transitions or derivation_algorithm is modified. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Medical coding dictionary used for this mapping when derivation_type is 'coded'. MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) for adverse events and medical history; WHO-DD (WHO Drug Dictionary) for concomitant medications; CTCAE (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) for severity grading. 'none' if no coding dictionary applies.
reference: MedDRA; WHO-DD; CTCAE; ICH E2A; FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: Version of the medical coding dictionary applied for this mapping (e.g., MedDRA v26.1, WHO-DD March 2023). Ensures reproducibility of coded terms across transformation runs and supports regulatory submission traceability.
reference: MedDRA; WHO-DD; ICH E2A; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

business_glossary_term: CDISC Controlled Terminology Code List Name
description: Name of the CDISC Controlled Terminology code list applied to this SDTM variable (e.g., 'AESEV', 'NCOMPLT', 'SEX', 'RACE'). Null if no controlled terminology applies. Governs permissible values for the target variable in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Date and time when this SDTM mapping rule record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance. Immutable after initial record creation.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Version of the CDISC Controlled Terminology package applied for this mapping (e.g., '2023-09-29'). Ensures reproducibility of coded values across transformation runs and regulatory submissions. Critical for FDA/EMA submission compliance.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

description: Supplementary comment text to be included in the CDISC Define-XML v2.1 submission package for this variable. Provides additional context for FDA/EMA reviewers about the derivation logic, data source, or special handling. Appears in the define.xml ItemDef Comment attribute.
reference: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Origin attribute value for this variable as it will appear in the CDISC Define-XML v2.1 submission metadata. Indicates the source of the data: 'CRF' (collected on eCRF), 'Derived' (algorithmically derived), 'Assigned' (assigned by sponsor/CRO), 'Protocol' (defined in protocol), 'eDT' (electronic data transfer), 'Predecessor' (derived from prior SDTM variable).
reference: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Full specification of the transformation logic or derivation rule applied to produce the target SDTM variable value from the source field(s). Includes SAS code snippets, conditional logic, date calculations, concatenation rules, and multi-source merge logic. For direct mappings, states 'Direct mapping from {source_field_name}'. Supports reproducible and auditable CDISC data transformation per ALCOA+ principles.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; SAS Drug Development

description: Classification of the mapping derivation method: 'direct' (verbatim copy from source), 'derived' (computed from one or more source fields), 'assigned' (constant or protocol-defined value), 'predecessor' (derived from a previously mapped SDTM variable), 'computed' (algorithmic calculation), 'coded' (medical coding via MedDRA or WHO-DD lookup).
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Date after which this version of the mapping rule is no longer active and has been superseded or deprecated. Null for currently active mapping rules. Supports temporal versioning of mapping specifications across protocol amendments.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Date from which this version of the mapping rule is effective and applicable to SDTM transformation runs. Supports version-controlled mapping specifications where different versions apply to different data collection periods or protocol amendments.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether this SDTM variable mapping requires data from more than one source field or form (True) or derives from a single source field (False). When True, the derivation_algorithm field documents all contributing source fields and the combination logic.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether the predecessor variable dependency documented in predecessor_variable is a hard requirement (True) that must be resolved before this mapping executes, or an informational dependency (False). Governs transformation program execution sequencing.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development

description: Indicates whether the target SDTM variable contains sensitive subject data requiring special handling under GDPR, HIPAA, or sponsor data privacy agreements (True). Examples include subject identifiers, dates of birth, and geographic data. Governs data masking and de-identification procedures in submission datasets.
reference: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

description: Date and time when this SDTM mapping rule record was most recently updated. Updated on every change to the mapping rule, derivation logic, or status. Supports change tracking and ALCOA+ audit trail requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code identifying this mapping rule within the study's SDTM mapping specification document. Follows the pattern MAP-{DOMAIN}-{VARIABLE}-{SEQUENCE}. Used in Data Management Plans (DMP) and CDISC submission packages.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Current lifecycle state of this SDTM mapping rule. Controls which version is active for production CDISC transformation runs. 'approved' rules are eligible for DBL and regulatory submission. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|in_review|approved|deprecated|superseded|on_hold — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11

description: Version number of this mapping rule in major.minor format (e.g., 1.0, 2.3). Incremented when the transformation logic, source field, or controlled terminology mapping changes. Supports version-controlled, auditable CDISC data transformation per ALCOA+ principles.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Free-text field for additional programmer or reviewer notes about this mapping rule, including special handling instructions, known data quality issues, sponsor-specific requirements, or cross-references to related mapping rules. Not included in regulatory submission artifacts.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Name of the SDTM variable (within the same or a different domain) that must be derived before this mapping can be executed. Documents derivation dependencies for sequencing transformation programs. Format: '{DOMAIN}.{VARIABLE}' (e.g., 'AE.AEDECOD'). Null if no predecessor dependency exists.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development

description: Name or employee identifier of the Data Management or Biostatistics reviewer who reviewed and approved this mapping rule. Supports dual-review traceability and ALCOA+ compliance for the SDTM mapping specification document.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Two-letter CDISC SDTM domain code identifying the target dataset domain (e.g., DM, AE, LB, VS, CM, EX, MH, DS, SV, TU). Determines the SDTM class and required/expected variable set for this mapping. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DM|AE|LB|VS|CM|EX|MH|DS|SV|TU|EC|FA|RS|TR|TU|PR|CE|DD|HO|ML|PC|PP|RE|RP|SR|SS|TI|TS|TV — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology

description: Version of the CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide that governs this mapping rule (e.g., 'SDTMIG v3.4', 'SDTMIG-AP v1.0'). Ensures regulatory submission compliance with the correct CDISC standard version as required by FDA and EMA data submission guidelines.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

description: CDISC core designation indicating whether the target SDTM variable is Required (Req), Expected (Exp), or Permissible (Perm) for the domain. Required variables must be populated; Expected variables should be populated when data is collected; Permissible variables are optional.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Human-readable descriptive label for the target SDTM variable as defined in the CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide (e.g., 'Dictionary-Derived Term', 'Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units'). Used in SAS dataset metadata and regulatory submission define.xml.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Name of the target CDISC SDTM variable within the specified domain (e.g., AEDECOD, LBSTRESN, VSORRES). Must conform to CDISC SDTM naming conventions: uppercase, 2–8 characters, domain prefix for most variables. This is the column name in the final SDTM dataset submitted to regulatory agencies.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: CDISC-defined role of the target SDTM variable within its domain class (Identifier, Topic, Qualifier, Timing, Rule). Determines how the variable functions within the SDTM dataset structure and governs its position and usage in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4

description: CDISC-defined data type of the target SDTM variable. 'Char' for character/text variables and 'Num' for numeric variables, as specified in the SDTM Implementation Guide and define.xml metadata. Governs SAS dataset column type in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Ordinal sequence number of this mapping rule within the parent SDTM dataset specification. Governs the order in which variables appear in the SDTM dataset and define.xml, and the execution order of transformation programs in SAS Drug Development.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Name of the raw/staging dataset (SAS dataset or EDC extract table) that contains the source field prior to SDTM transformation (e.g., 'RAW_AE', 'RAW_VS'). Used in SAS Drug Development transformation programs to identify the input dataset for each mapping rule.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Indicates whether this variable is mapped to a CDISC SDTM Supplemental Qualifier (SUPP--) dataset rather than the parent domain dataset (True). SUPPQUAL datasets hold non-standard variables that cannot be accommodated in the standard domain structure.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Short variable name (QNAM) used in the SUPPQUAL dataset for this non-standard variable. Populated only when suppqual_flag is True. Must be uppercase, 1–8 characters, and unique within the SUPPQUAL dataset for the domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4

description: Pinnacle 21 / CDISC conformance rule error or warning code associated with the most recent validation failure for this mapping (e.g., 'SD0083', 'SD0006'). Null when validation_status is 'passed' or 'not_validated'. Supports targeted remediation by the CDISC programmer.
reference: CDISC Conformance Rules; Pinnacle 21; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Current status of the CDISC Pinnacle 21 / OpenCDISC validation check result for this mapping rule. 'passed' indicates no conformance errors; 'failed' indicates outstanding validation errors requiring remediation before DBL; 'waived' indicates a documented exception approved by the Data Management team.
reference: CDISC Conformance Rules; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; Pinnacle 21

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Mean accuracy of the assay expressed as percent of nominal concentration (%Nominal) at QC levels during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically 85–115% (80–120% at LLOQ). Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Broad classification of the analyte type measured by the assay. Distinguishes small molecule drugs (PK), large molecule biologics, biomarkers (PD), immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies), metabolites, and endogenous compounds. Drives regulatory submission strategy and validation requirements.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Name of the substance being measured by the assay (e.g., drug compound, metabolite, biomarker, anti-drug antibody). Directly links the assay to the pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), or immunogenicity endpoint it supports.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the assay by the bioanalytical laboratory or sponsor (e.g., 'BA-LC-001', 'ELISA-TNF-003'). Used as the business identifier across CTMS, EDC, and regulatory submissions. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011)

description: Full descriptive name of the bioanalytical assay as used in study protocols, validation reports, and regulatory submissions (e.g., 'LC-MS/MS Assay for Compound XYZ in Human Plasma'). Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE IDENTITY_LABEL category.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Primary scientific purpose the assay serves within the clinical or nonclinical program. PK (Pharmacokinetics) assays measure drug concentration over time; PD (Pharmacodynamics) assays measure biological effect; Immunogenicity assays detect anti-drug antibodies; DMPK (Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics) assays support metabolite profiling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PK|PD|Immunogenicity|Safety Biomarker|Efficacy Biomarker|DMPK|Other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Analytical technology platform used to perform the assay. Common types include LC-MS/MS (Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry), ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay), ECL (Electrochemiluminescence), PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction), Flow Cytometry, and LBA (Ligand Binding Assay). Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: LC-MS/MS|ELISA|ECL|PCR|Flow Cytometry|LBA|HPLC|GC-MS|Western Blot|IHC|CLIA|RIA — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Mathematical regression model used to fit the calibration curve for back-calculation of analyte concentrations from instrument response. Common models include Linear (1/x or 1/x² weighting), Quadratic, 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL), and 5-Parameter Logistic (5PL) for LBA methods.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Standardized test code from the CDISC Controlled Terminology for the SDTM PC (Pharmacokinetics Concentrations) or LB (Laboratory Test Results) domain. Enables direct mapping of assay results to CDISC SDTM datasets for regulatory submission.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA SDTM Submission Requirements

description: Timestamp when the bioanalytical assay record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

description: Statistical method used to establish the screening and confirmatory cut points for immunogenicity (anti-drug antibody) assays (e.g., 'Parametric 5th percentile', 'Non-parametric 5th percentile'). Applicable only to immunogenicity assays; null for PK/PD assays.
reference: FDA Immunogenicity Testing Guidance (2019); EMA Guideline on Immunogenicity Assessment; ICH M10

description: Maximum validated dilution factor that can be applied to samples exceeding the ULOQ while maintaining assay accuracy and precision within acceptance criteria. Samples requiring dilution beyond this factor must be flagged.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Date after which the assay validation is no longer considered current and re-validation or re-qualification is required. Relevant for long-running studies where assay reagents, reference standards, or critical reagents may expire.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether the assay is performed under Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards as required for clinical trial sample analysis. True = GCP-compliant; False = non-GCP. Distinct from GLP compliance — clinical samples require GCP; nonclinical samples require GLP.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

description: Indicates whether the assay was validated and is performed under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for nonclinical safety studies submitted to regulatory agencies. True = GLP-compliant; False = non-GLP.
reference: GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD Principles of GLP; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Between-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) across multiple analytical runs during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV). Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Name or identifier of the internal standard (IS) used in the assay for quantification normalization (e.g., stable isotope-labeled analog, structural analog). Critical for LC-MS/MS and other chromatographic methods to correct for matrix effects and extraction variability.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Within-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) at the QC concentration levels, as determined during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV), or ≤20% at LLOQ. Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Lower Limit of Quantification — the lowest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified with acceptable accuracy and precision per the validated method. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit. Critical for PK/PD data interpretation and regulatory submission. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

description: Unit of measurement for the LLOQ and ULOQ values (e.g., 'ng/mL', 'pg/mL', 'µg/mL', 'nM'). Must be consistent with the unit reported in PK/PD concentration data submitted to regulatory agencies.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Number of days for which analyte stability in the biological matrix at long-term storage conditions (typically -20°C or -70°C) has been validated. Samples stored beyond this period require re-validation of stability before results can be reported.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether matrix effect (ion suppression/enhancement for LC-MS/MS; non-specific binding for LBA) was formally evaluated during validation. True = matrix effect experiments conducted; False = not assessed.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Biological matrix in which the analyte is measured (e.g., plasma, serum, whole blood, urine, cerebrospinal fluid). The assay is validated specifically for the declared matrix; use in a different matrix requires re-validation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Plasma|Serum|Whole Blood|Urine|CSF|Tissue|Saliva|Feces|Synovial Fluid|Bronchoalveolar Lavage|Dried Blood Spot — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether parallelism (serial dilution of incurred samples producing results parallel to the calibration curve) was assessed. Relevant primarily for LBA and immunogenicity assays. True = parallelism assessed; False = not assessed.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Lot number of the certified reference standard used to prepare calibration standards and quality control (QC) samples. Traceability of the reference standard lot is required for regulatory submissions and audit purposes.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); USP Reference Standards; ICH M10

description: Minimum volume of biological matrix (in microliters) required per sample aliquot for a single assay run. Used for specimen collection planning, biobank management, and feasibility assessment of retrospective analyses.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; CDISC SDTM BS Domain

description: Indicates whether selectivity (absence of interference from endogenous matrix components) was formally assessed during validation. True = selectivity experiments conducted and documented; False = not assessed. Required for full validation per FDA/EMA/ICH M10.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Biological species for which the assay has been validated. Assays validated in human matrices may differ from those validated in preclinical animal species used in DMPK studies. Drives applicability to clinical vs. nonclinical programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Human|Rat|Mouse|Dog|Monkey|Rabbit|Other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; OECD GLP Principles

description: Sponsor-assigned identifier for the assay as referenced in the study protocol, SAP, or regulatory submission. May differ from the CRO's internal assay code. Required for cross-referencing sponsor documents with CRO laboratory records.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA IND (21 CFR Part 312); CDISC SDTM

description: Number of freeze-thaw cycles for which analyte stability in the biological matrix has been validated. Samples subjected to more freeze-thaw cycles than validated must be flagged or excluded from analysis.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Required storage temperature and conditions for samples analyzed by this assay (e.g., '-70°C ± 10°C', '-20°C', '2–8°C'). Defines the chain-of-custody storage requirement for clinical samples to maintain analyte integrity.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; ICH Q1A Stability Testing

description: Assay code of the newer version that replaces this assay when it is retired or superseded. Supports version lineage tracking and ensures historical sample results can be linked to the correct assay version.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; ALCOA+

description: Upper Limit of Quantification — the highest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified within the validated dynamic range. Samples above ULOQ must be diluted and re-assayed. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the bioanalytical assay record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles. Tracks when assay parameters, validation status, or metadata were last changed.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

description: Indicates whether this certification is recognized under a mutual recognition agreement between regulatory authorities (e.g., FDA-EMA, OECD GLP MAD). True = recognized under MRA; False = jurisdiction-specific only. Relevant for multi-regional clinical trials.
reference: OECD GLP Mutual Acceptance of Data (MAD); FDA-EMA Mutual Recognition Agreement; ICH E6(R2)

description: Number of calendar days before the expiry date at which automated renewal notifications should be triggered. Configurable per certification type and issuing authority requirements (e.g., 90 days for CLIA, 180 days for GLP).
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl Document Control

description: Certificate number of the immediately preceding certification record that this record renews or supersedes. Enables chain-of-custody traceability across certification renewal cycles.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

description: Outcome of the most recent proficiency testing or EQA survey associated with this certification. SATISFACTORY = passed; UNSATISFACTORY = failed one or more analytes; UNSUCCESSFUL = failed to meet minimum passing threshold; PENDING = results not yet received; NOT_APPLICABLE = no proficiency testing required for this certification type.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 Subpart H; CAP Proficiency Testing; ISO 15189

description: Timestamp when this certification record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this certification record in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data currency monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

description: Reference number or dossier identifier for any regulatory submission (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, CTD/eCTD) in which this laboratory certification was included as supporting documentation.
reference: FDA IND 21 CFR Part 312; FDA NDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA MAA; ICH CTD; eCTD

description: Date on which a previously suspended certification was reinstated by the issuing authority following successful corrective action. Null if the certification has never been suspended or has not yet been reinstated.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

description: Target date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the issuing authority to maintain uninterrupted certification status. Typically calculated as a fixed lead time before the expiry date per issuing authority requirements.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; CAP Accreditation; ISO 15189

description: Current status of the certification renewal process. Tracks the renewal workflow from initiation through approval or rejection. NOT_REQUIRED applies to certifications that do not have a periodic renewal cycle.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA/Document Control

description: Actual date on which the renewal application was submitted to the issuing authority. Used to confirm timely submission and support audit trail requirements.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

description: Name of the authorized signatory from the issuing authority who signed or approved the certificate. Supports audit trail and certificate authenticity verification.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58

description: Operational system of record from which this certification record was sourced or ingested (e.g., MasterControl document control, Veeva Vault eTMF, Oracle Siebel CTMS, or manually entered). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (MasterControl, Veeva Vault, CTMS). Enables traceability back to the source system for reconciliation and audit purposes per ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

description: Standardized code identifying the laboratory specialty or discipline covered by this certification, aligned with CLIA specialty categories or equivalent regulatory classification (e.g., HEMATOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, MICROBIOLOGY, IMMUNOLOGY, TOXICOLOGY, MOLECULAR_PATHOLOGY).
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 Subpart C; CAP Accreditation Checklists; ISO 15189

description: Date on which the certification was suspended, revoked, or withdrawn. Populated only when certification_status is SUSPENDED, REVOKED, or WITHDRAWN. Supports regulatory compliance and audit trail.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

description: Reason provided by the issuing authority or the laboratory for suspension, revocation, or withdrawal of the certification. Populated only when certification_status is SUSPENDED, REVOKED, or WITHDRAWN.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; ICH E6(R2)

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the laboratory facility record. Primary key for the lab_facility data product. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: ISO 15189; CLIA (42 CFR Part 493); CAP Accreditation Standards

description: Primary street address line of the laboratory facility. Used for specimen shipment labels, regulatory correspondence, and audit documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA; CAP Accreditation Standards

description: Secondary address line (suite, floor, building) for the laboratory facility. Supplements address_line1 for complete mailing and shipment address.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility has certified long-term specimen storage (biobanking) capabilities, including controlled-temperature archival storage. Relevant for studies requiring retained samples for future exploratory analyses.
reference: ISBER Best Practices for Repositories; ISO 20387:2018; ICH E6(R2) GCP

business_glossary_term: College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation Number
description: Accreditation number issued by the College of American Pathologists (CAP) confirming the laboratory meets rigorous quality standards. Widely recognized by sponsors and regulatory agencies as evidence of laboratory quality. Null if not CAP-accredited.
reference: CAP Accreditation Program Standards; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance for Industry

description: City in which the laboratory facility is physically located. Used for geographic reporting, logistics planning, and specimen shipment routing.
reference: ISO 3166-2; GDPR Article 4; ICH E6(R2) GCP

business_glossary_term: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Certificate Number
description: Federal CLIA certificate number issued by CMS to U.S. clinical laboratories authorizing them to perform testing on human specimens. Required for regulatory compliance and sponsor qualification audits. Null for non-U.S. facilities.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CMS CLIA Program; FDA 21 CFR Part 58

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the country in which the laboratory facility is physically located (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Drives regulatory jurisdiction determination and applicable accreditation standards.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 44; HIPAA

description: Timestamp when the laboratory facility record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) Analysis Capability Flag
description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility is equipped and validated to perform Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) analyses, including metabolite profiling and enzyme characterization studies.
reference: FDA Guidance on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2018); ICH M10; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Standardized laboratory code used in electronic data interchange (EDI) transmissions between the laboratory and EDC/CTMS systems. Aligns with CDISC LAB data standards for lab results transfer.
reference: CDISC LAB Data Standard; HL7 FHIR; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique business identifier for the laboratory facility (e.g., 'LAB-CENT-001'). Used in study protocols, eCRFs, and regulatory submissions to reference the facility. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.
reference: CDISC SDTM IG; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 58

description: Official legal or operating name of the laboratory facility as registered with accreditation bodies and regulatory authorities. Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.
reference: ISO 15189:2022; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Classification of the laboratory facility by its operational role in clinical trials. Central labs process specimens from multiple sites; local labs are site-affiliated; bioanalytical labs perform assay development and sample analysis; PK/DMPK labs focus on pharmacokinetics and drug metabolism. Serves as CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM LB Domain; FDA Guidance on Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility has validated flow cytometry capabilities for immunophenotyping and cell-based assays, commonly required in oncology and immunology trials.
reference: ISO 15189:2022; CAP Accreditation Standards; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility holds a current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification or has been qualified under GCP guidelines by the sponsor or CRO. Required for laboratories participating in regulated clinical trials.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility is equipped to perform genomic analyses (e.g., PCR, NGS, genotyping) relevant to pharmacogenomics endpoints in clinical trials.
reference: ICH E15 Pharmacogenomics; FDA Guidance on Pharmacogenomics; ISO 15189:2022

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility is certified under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations, required for non-clinical safety studies and certain bioanalytical work supporting regulatory submissions.
reference: OECD GLP Principles; FDA 21 CFR Part 58; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Certificate number issued by a national accreditation body (e.g., UKAS, DAkkS, COFRAC) confirming the laboratory conforms to ISO 15189 requirements for medical laboratories. Recognized internationally for cross-border clinical trial operations.
reference: ISO 15189:2022; ILAC P15; EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Unique identifier for this facility within its Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for electronic data exchange, specimen tracking, and results transmission to EDC systems such as Medidata Rave.
reference: CDISC LAB Data Standard; 21 CFR Part 11; GAMP 5; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Name of the LIMS software vendor used by the facility (e.g., LabVantage, STARLIMS, LabWare). Relevant for EDC integration planning and data transfer agreement scoping.
reference: CDISC LAB Data Standard; 21 CFR Part 11; GAMP 5

description: Full name of the licensed physician or doctoral scientist serving as the laboratory's Medical Director, as required by CLIA and CAP accreditation. Accountable for overall laboratory quality and regulatory compliance.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493.1441; CAP Accreditation Standards; ISO 15189:2022 Section 4.1

description: Name of the central laboratory network or parent organization to which this facility belongs (e.g., 'Covance', 'Q2 Solutions', 'BioReference', 'PPD'). Used for contract management, network-level performance reporting, and escalation routing.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.2; ISO 9001:2015

description: Description of the laboratory facility's standard operating hours (e.g., 'Mon-Fri 07:00-19:00 EST'). Used for specimen shipment scheduling, turnaround time SLA definition, and site coordinator guidance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 15189:2022 Section 4.1

description: Current lifecycle state of the laboratory facility indicating whether it is actively accepting specimens for clinical trial studies. Drives eligibility for new study assignments and site qualification workflows. Serves as LIFECYCLE_STATUS per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; ISO 15189:2022; CAP Accreditation Standards

description: Indicates whether the laboratory facility is equipped and validated to perform pharmacokinetic (PK) sample analysis, including bioanalytical assays for drug concentration measurement.
reference: FDA Guidance on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation; ICH M10

description: Postal or ZIP code of the laboratory facility's physical address. Used for specimen shipment logistics and geographic analysis.
reference: ISO 3166-1; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA

description: Name of the preferred or contracted courier service for specimen shipment to this facility (e.g., 'World Courier', 'Marken', 'FedEx Custom Critical'). Used for logistics planning and chain-of-custody documentation.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 15189:2022 Section 5.4

description: Email address of the primary operational contact at the laboratory facility. Used for study coordination communications, specimen shipment notifications, and results transmission alerts.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Full name of the primary operational contact person at the laboratory facility (e.g., Laboratory Director or Operations Manager). Used for study coordination, issue escalation, and regulatory correspondence.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; CAP Accreditation Standards

description: Primary telephone number for the laboratory facility's operational contact. Used for urgent specimen handling queries, critical value notifications, and logistics coordination.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA

description: Date on which the sponsor or CRO qualification of the laboratory facility expires, requiring re-qualification before the facility can be assigned to new studies.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.2; FDA Guidance on Vendor Qualification

description: Sponsor or CRO qualification status of the laboratory facility, reflecting the outcome of vendor qualification audits and ongoing performance reviews. Determines whether the facility may be assigned to new studies.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.2; FDA Guidance on Vendor Qualification; ISO 9001:2015

description: Comma-separated list of additional regulatory certifications held by the facility beyond primary accreditation (e.g., 'FDA-registered, EMA-compliant, PMDA-approved, NY State DOH'). Supports multi-jurisdictional study eligibility assessment.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 493; EMA GCP Directive; PMDA Guidelines; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Maximum number of specimens the facility can process per business day under normal operating conditions. Used for capacity planning, site feasibility assessments, and study logistics. Serves as MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 15189:2022 Section 4.1

description: Latest time of day (HH:MM, 24-hour format, local facility time) by which specimens must be received to be processed on the same business day. Critical for study protocol logistics and turnaround time commitments.
reference: ISO 15189:2022; CAP Accreditation Standards; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: State, province, or region in which the laboratory facility is physically located. Used for regulatory jurisdiction mapping and logistics.
reference: ISO 3166-2; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA

description: IANA time zone identifier for the laboratory facility's local time (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Used for specimen receipt timestamp normalization, turnaround time calculations, and critical value notification SLA tracking.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM

description: Standard turnaround time in hours from specimen receipt to results availability for routine panels. Used in study feasibility assessments and service level agreement (SLA) monitoring.
reference: ISO 15189:2022 Section 5.8; CAP Accreditation Standards; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Turnaround time in hours for STAT (urgent) specimen processing. Used for safety monitoring protocols where rapid results are required for subject safety decisions.
reference: ISO 15189:2022 Section 5.8; CAP Accreditation Standards; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Timestamp when the laboratory facility record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Primary key for the lab_qualification association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the clinical development program for which this laboratory facility is qualified.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the laboratory facility being qualified for this clinical program.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Reference identifier for the vendor contract or master service agreement governing the laboratory facility's engagement for this clinical program. Links to the procurement or legal contract management system.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Indicates whether this laboratory facility is designated as the primary (central) laboratory for this clinical program. A program may have one primary lab and multiple specialty or backup labs.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Date on which the laboratory facility was formally qualified to perform specimen analysis for this clinical program. Marks the start of the approved engagement for regulatory audit trail purposes.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Current sponsor or CRO qualification status of the laboratory facility for this specific clinical program. Reflects the outcome of the qualification assessment and drives whether the lab may receive specimens for this program.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP vendor qualification standards

description: Narrative or structured description of the specific assay panels, specimen types, and analytical services this laboratory facility is approved to perform for this clinical program (e.g., hematology, PK assays, biomarker panels).
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Date on which the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor formally approved this laboratory facility for use in this clinical program. May differ from qualification_date when sponsor review follows CRO qualification.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

business_glossary_term: Lab Service Contract - Lab Service Contract Id
description: Primary key for the lab_service_contract association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Lab Service Contract - Lab Facility Id
description: Foreign key linking to the laboratory facility engaged under this service contract.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Lab Service Contract - Study Budget Id
description: Foreign key linking to the study budget under which this lab facility is contracted.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Sequential integer tracking the number of amendments applied to this lab service contract record. Incremented each time contracted_rate, service_scope, or terms are formally revised. Supports audit trail for SOX-compliant budget change management.
Current lifecycle state of this lab service contract record. Drives workflow approvals and determines whether the facility is authorized to invoice against this study budget.

The negotiated unit rate agreed with the lab facility for specimen processing services under this specific study budget. Varies per facility-study combination and cannot reside on either the facility master or the budget master alone.
reference: ISO 4217 currency context via currency_code

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the contracted_rate. May differ from the study budget's base currency when the lab facility is in a different country.
reference: ISO 4217

description: The date from which the contracted terms between this lab facility and this study budget become financially binding. Used for cost accrual timing and sponsor invoicing alignment.
The date on which the contracted terms expire or are superseded by an amendment. Supports contract lifecycle management and budget re-forecasting.

Narrative or structured description of the assay panels, specimen types, and analytical services covered under this facility-budget contract. Defines what the lab is authorized and budgeted to perform for this study.
Unique surrogate identifier for the laboratory collection kit master record. Primary key for the lab_kit entity.
reference: CDISC SDTM; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Lab kit approval by a sponsor employee is a required step before kit deployment to sites, supporting regulatory inspection readiness. The existing approved_by plain-text column is a denormalized emplo
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: A laboratory collection kit is supplied by and associated with a specific central laboratory facility. The central_lab_code STRING column is a denormalized reference to lab_facility. Adding lab_facili
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the laboratory panel definition that this kit is designed to support. Ensures correct collection materials are used per protocol-specified assays.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain; ICH E6(R2)

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Lab kits are designed and versioned per protocol specification (tube types, volumes, handling instructions). Regulatory inspections and GCP audits require tracing kit versions to the protocol that man
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to agreement.scope_of_work. Business justification: The SOW specifies lab kit types, quantities per visit, and per-site supply requirements. Lab supply chain teams reconcile actual kit inventory and usage against SOW commitments to identify scope gaps
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to agreement.study_contract. Business justification: Lab kit procurement and supply is governed by the study contract as a pass-through cost item. Supply chain and finance teams track kit costs against contracted budgets and validate kit supply invoices
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this kit is designated. Links the kit to a specific protocol and sponsor.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Protocol amendments that change specimen collection requirements trigger new kit versions. Tracing kit versions to the driving amendment is required for amendment impact tracking, site resupply planni
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical site to which this kit is assigned or shipped. Supports site-level inventory tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Date on which the kit design and components list was formally approved by the sponsor or quality team for use in the study. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; MasterControl QMS; Veeva Vault

description: IATA/UN biohazard classification for shipping the collected specimen (Category A UN2814, Category B UN3373, Exempt). Determines packaging and shipping documentation requirements for specimen transport.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations P650; UN Model Regulations; WHO Guidance on Regulations for the Transport of Infectious Substances

description: CDISC SDTM controlled terminology value for specimen type (LBSPEC variable), e.g., BLOOD, URINE, PLASMA, SERUM. Enables direct mapping to SDTM LB domain for regulatory submission datasets.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Specific timepoint within a visit at which the specimen should be collected (e.g., pre-dose, 1h post-dose, 4h post-dose). Particularly relevant for PK/PD sampling schedules.
reference: CDISC SDTM LBTPTNUM; ICH E6(R2); FDA Bioanalytical Method Guidance

description: Free-text or structured description of all components included in the kit (e.g., EDTA tubes, serum separator tubes, cryovials, dry ice packs, biohazard bags, requisition forms, instruction leaflets). Supports site training and deviation investigation.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; CDISC SDTM

description: Timestamp when the lab kit master record was first created in the system. Part of the mandatory audit trail for GCP compliance and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

description: Date after which the kit must not be used for specimen collection. Expiry is driven by the stability of collection tubes, preservatives, and reagents. Sites must discard or return kits past this date.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 15189; 21 CFR Part 211; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether the subject must be fasting prior to specimen collection using this kit. Fasting status affects reference ranges and result interpretation for metabolic and lipid panels.
reference: CDISC SDTM LBFAST; ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189

description: Version number of the collection instruction leaflet included in the kit. Ensures site staff follow the correct collection procedure aligned to the current protocol version.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether this kit is an ancillary/backup kit (True) rather than a primary protocol-required kit (False). Ancillary kits are used for repeat collections or unscheduled assessments.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Functional category of the kit indicating the scientific purpose of the specimen collection (e.g., Pharmacokinetics (PK), Pharmacodynamics (PD), safety labs, biomarker, genetic). Aligns kit to the study's analytical objectives. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pk|pd|safety|biomarker|genetic|microbiome|dmpk|other — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM LBCAT; ICH E6(R2)

description: ISO 639 language code for the primary language of the kit label and instruction leaflet (e.g., en, fr, de, ja). Ensures regulatory compliance for multi-country trials requiring local language labelling.
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA; Health Canada; ICH E6(R2); ISO 639

description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to the kit, typically printed on the kit label and used for chain-of-custody tracking. Corresponds to the kit barcode or label ID in RTSM/IRT systems such as Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Current lifecycle status of the kit. Drives inventory management workflows and ensures expired or quarantined kits are not used for specimen collection. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: available|assigned|shipped|received|used|expired|quarantined|destroyed|returned — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Classification of the kit by specimen matrix type (e.g., blood, urine, tissue). Determines the collection containers and preservatives included. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: blood|urine|saliva|tissue|csf|stool|buccal_swab|plasma|serum|other — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM LBSPEC; ISO 15189

description: Version identifier of the kit design or configuration. Used to track protocol amendments that change collection requirements, ensuring sites use the correct kit version per the current protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Accreditation standard under which the central laboratory processing specimens from this kit is certified (e.g., ISO 15189, CAP, CLIA, GCLP). Required for regulatory submissions and sponsor quality oversight.
reference: ISO 15189; CAP; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; GCLP Guidelines; ICH E6(R2)

description: Manufacturing lot number assigned by the kit supplier or central laboratory. Enables traceability for quality investigations, recalls, and regulatory inspections. Critical for ALCOA+ compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 15189

description: Date on which the kit was manufactured or assembled by the supplier. Used in conjunction with expiry date to calculate shelf life and manage inventory rotation.
reference: ISO 15189; 21 CFR Part 211; ICH E6(R2)

description: Type of preservative or additive included in the kit (e.g., EDTA, heparin, sodium fluoride, formalin, RNAlater). Critical for specimen stability and downstream analytical method compatibility.
reference: ISO 15189; CLSI; CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD

description: Protocol-defined visit name or visit window for which this kit is intended (e.g., Screening, Day 1, Week 4). Ensures the correct kit type is used at the correct study visit per the protocol schedule of assessments.
reference: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM VISITNUM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Standard number of kits included in a single shipment to a site. Used for supply planning, purchase order generation, and site inventory management.
reference: ICH E6(R2); SAP S/4HANA Supply Chain; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Minimum quantity of kits at a site below which a resupply order should be triggered. Supports proactive inventory management to prevent site stock-outs.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; SAP S/4HANA

description: Indicates whether a laboratory requisition form (paper or pre-printed label) is included in the kit. Requisition forms are required by central labs for specimen processing and chain-of-custody documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether the used kit or residual materials must be returned to the central laboratory or sponsor after specimen collection. Relevant for chain-of-custody and waste management compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations

description: Operational system of record from which this kit record originated (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM, Oracle Clinical One, Oracle Siebel CTMS). Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the lakehouse.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; CDISC Data Exchange Standards

description: Free-text field capturing any special handling requirements for the kit or collected specimen (e.g., protect from light, invert tube 8 times, centrifuge within 30 minutes, ship on dry ice). Critical for specimen integrity.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; IATA P650; CLSI

description: Categorical storage condition required for the kit (e.g., refrigerated 2–8°C, frozen −20°C, room temperature). Complements the numeric temperature range with a human-readable label for site staff.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; IATA P650

description: Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the kit. Used alongside minimum temperature to define the acceptable storage range and trigger excursion alerts.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations

description: Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the kit. Ensures cold-chain integrity and preservative efficacy. Deviations must be documented per GCP.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations

description: Supplier's own catalog or part number for this kit configuration. Used for reordering, purchase orders in SAP S/4HANA, and supplier quality documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ISO 15189; ICH E6(R2)

description: Name of the vendor or central laboratory that manufactured and supplied the kit. Used for procurement, quality investigations, and supplier qualification tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189; SAP S/4HANA Procurement

description: Total number of collection tubes included in the kit. Used for inventory reconciliation and to verify completeness of kit contents upon receipt at the site.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 15189

description: Type of collection tube(s) included in the kit (e.g., EDTA K2, SST, lithium heparin, sodium citrate, PAXgene). Determines anticoagulant or additive present, which is critical for assay validity.
reference: CDISC SDTM LBSPEC; ISO 15189; CLSI GP44

description: Nominal volume in millilitres of each collection tube in the kit. Used to confirm adequate sample volume for the required assays and to flag insufficient sample at processing.
reference: ISO 15189; CLSI GP44; CDISC SDTM

description: Timestamp when the lab kit master record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

description: Indicates whether this stratification factor is included as a covariate in the primary statistical analysis model (True) or is used only for randomization balance without inclusion in the primary analysis (False). Relevant for ANCOVA and CMH test specifications in the SAP.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Covariate Adjustment; CDISC ADaM; SAP

description: Total number of enumerated levels (strata) defined for this stratification factor. Drives the dimensionality of the stratification matrix and the number of randomization lists required. For example, a 3-region factor has level_count = 3.

description: The maximum allowable imbalance (as a percentage or absolute count, per unit_of_imbalance) between treatment arms within any stratum defined by this factor before a balancing action is triggered in the minimization algorithm.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; SAP

description: Specific variant of the minimization algorithm applied for this factor: 'pocock_simon' for the Pocock-Simon method, 'weighted_minimization' for factor-weighted minimization, 'biased_coin' for biased-coin minimization, 'deterministic' for deterministic minimization, 'none' if minimization is not applicable.
reference: ICH E9; Pocock-Simon (1975); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Numeric weight assigned to this stratification factor in a minimization or weighted minimization algorithm (e.g., Pocock-Simon). Values typically range from 0.0 to 1.0, with higher weights indicating greater influence on treatment allocation balance. Null if minimization is not used.
reference: ICH E9; Pocock-Simon Minimization Algorithm; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Defines the RTSM system behavior when the stratification factor value is missing or unknown at the time of randomization: 'block_randomization' to prevent randomization, 'assign_default_level' to use a pre-specified default level, 'flag_and_hold' to alert the site, 'exclude_from_minimization' to proceed without this factor.
reference: ICH E9; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; SAP

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, biostatistician comments, or RTSM configuration remarks related to this stratification factor that do not fit into structured fields. Not used for regulatory submissions.

description: Reference to the specific section of the study protocol document that defines this stratification factor (e.g., 'Section 8.2.1 Stratification Factors'). Enables traceability from the data model to the governing protocol.

description: The randomization algorithm applied in conjunction with this stratification factor: 'permuted_block' for block randomization within strata, 'minimization' for adaptive minimization, 'stratified_block' for stratified permuted block, 'dynamic_allocation' for covariate-adaptive methods.

description: The native identifier assigned to this stratification factor within the source RTSM/IRT system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM internal factor ID or Oracle Clinical One factor GUID). Used for system integration, reconciliation, and audit trail linkage.

description: The CDISC SDTM variable name that maps to this stratification factor for regulatory submission datasets (e.g., 'STRAT1', 'REGION1'). Used in SDTM TR/SUPPFA domains and ADaM ADSL derivations.

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version

description: Three-letter ISO 639-2 language code of the MedDRA dictionary used for coding (e.g., 'ENG' for English, 'JPN' for Japanese). Relevant for multi-regional studies where local language MedDRA versions may be used (e.g., PMDA submissions in Japan).

reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; CDISC DM Best Practices

business_glossary_term: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) Code

business_glossary_term: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) Name

reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLGT

description: Eight-digit MedDRA numeric code for the High Level Term (HLT) in the MedDRA hierarchy above the PT. Used for grouping related PTs in aggregate safety analyses and signal detection.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AEHLTCD

description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) corresponding to hlt_code. Supports mid-level grouping in safety tabulations and DSMB/DMC review packages.

description: Indicates whether the adverse event associated with this MedDRA coding record meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition). Drives expedited reporting timelines.

description: Descriptive text of the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) corresponding to pt_code. Used as the standard term in regulatory submissions, CIOMS forms, and safety narratives.

reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2A; CDISC SDTM CM domain

reference: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Outcome observed when the investigational product was withdrawn (dechallenged) following the adverse event. A positive dechallenge (AE resolved or improved upon withdrawal) supports a causal relationship. Captured per ICH E2A causality criteria.
reference: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Date
description: The date on which the DSMB/DMC formally reviewed this causality assessment during a scheduled or ad hoc safety review meeting.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DMC

business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reviewed Flag
description: Indicates whether this causality assessment was reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) as part of a formal safety review. Supports DSMB/DMC meeting documentation and regulatory oversight.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on DMC; EMA Reflection Paper on DMC

description: Determination of whether the adverse event is listed in the current Investigator's Brochure (IB) or Reference Safety Information (RSI) as a known effect of the investigational product. Drives SUSAR classification and expedited reporting obligations.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether this causality assessment triggers an obligation for expedited regulatory reporting (7-day or 15-day report) to health authorities such as FDA, EMA, or PMDA based on SUSAR classification.
reference: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether this causality assessment is a revision of a previously submitted assessment. True when the assessor has changed their causality determination after initial submission, triggering regulatory follow-up reporting obligations.
reference: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Free-text clinical narrative provided by the assessor explaining the reasoning behind the causality determination. Includes consideration of temporal relationship, biological plausibility, dechallenge/rechallenge results, and alternative explanations. Required for regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Outcome observed when the investigational product was re-administered (rechallenged) after the adverse event resolved. A positive rechallenge (AE recurred) provides strong evidence of causal relationship. Captured per ICH E2A causality criteria.
reference: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

description: Calculated deadline date by which the expedited regulatory report (SUSAR/IND safety report) must be submitted to health authorities. Derived from the date of first awareness plus the applicable reporting timeline.
reference: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The applicable expedited reporting timeline in calendar days from the date of first awareness of the SUSAR (typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening or 15 days for other serious unexpected reactions). Drives compliance monitoring.
reference: ICH E2A Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Sequential revision version number for this causality assessment. Starts at 1 for the original assessment and increments with each revision. Enables audit trail tracking of assessment changes over the case lifecycle.
reference: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Argus Safety versioning

description: Indicates whether this causality assessment has been flagged for inclusion in pharmacovigilance signal detection analysis within Oracle Argus Safety. Supports aggregate safety review and cumulative causality trend monitoring.
reference: ICH E2E; EMA GVP Module IX; FDA Guidance on Signal Detection

description: The native record identifier from the source system (Oracle Argus Safety case assessment ID or Medidata Rave record ID) for this causality assessment. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational system.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; CDISC SDTM

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this causality assessment record was extracted. Primarily Oracle Argus Safety; may include Medidata Rave for EDC-sourced assessments or 'manual' for paper-based entries.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles

description: The Sponsor Medical Monitor's independent causality determination, captured separately from the investigator's assessment. When sponsor_causality_override is True, this field holds the sponsor's differing conclusion used for regulatory reporting.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether the Sponsor Medical Monitor's causality determination differs from (overrides) the Investigator's assessment. When True, both assessments are retained and the sponsor's determination governs regulatory reporting obligations per ICH E2A.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR 312.32

business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
description: Indicates whether this adverse event has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) based on the combination of seriousness, causality (at least possible), and unexpectedness criteria. Triggers mandatory expedited regulatory reporting.
reference: ICH E2A; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Assessment of whether the timing between investigational product administration and adverse event onset is consistent with a causal relationship. A key criterion in WHO and ICH causality assessment frameworks.
reference: ICH E2A; WHO Causality Assessment Criteria; CIOMS

description: The date and time when this causality assessment record was most recently modified in the source system. Tracks the latest change for audit trail compliance and Silver layer incremental load processing.
reference: ICH E6(R2) ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5

description: WHO Drug Dictionary standardized drug code for the product (investigational or concomitant) being assessed. Enables cross-study signal detection and regulatory pharmacovigilance reporting.
reference: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD); ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each CTCAE grade definition record in the reference table. This is the primary key for the ctcae_grade product.
