reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: The official CTCAE adverse event term name as published by NCI (e.g., 'Atrial fibrillation', 'Nausea', 'Peripheral neuropathy'). This is the standardized clinical term used to classify and report adverse events across all clinical trials. Corresponds to the AETERM or AEDECOD field in CDISC SDTM AE domain and is the primary human-readable label for this grading record.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3 AE Domain; ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management

description: Specifies the patient population for which this CTCAE grade definition is applicable (e.g., 'All', 'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Oncology'). Some CTCAE terms and grade criteria differ by population (e.g., pediatric-specific grading criteria). Used to filter applicable grade definitions when assigning severity in studies with specific population constraints.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E11 Clinical Investigation of Medicinal Products in the Pediatric Population; FDA Pediatric Study Requirements

business_glossary_term: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Codelist Code
description: The CDISC controlled terminology codelist code associated with this CTCAE grade entry (e.g., the AETOXGR codelist code). Enables direct mapping to CDISC SDTM submission datasets and ADaM analysis datasets produced in SAS Drug Development. Required for eCTD regulatory submissions to FDA, EMA, and PMDA.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; CDISC ADaM IG; FDA eCTD Technical Specifications

description: A brief description of what changed in this grade definition relative to the prior CTCAE version (e.g., 'Grade 3 criteria updated to include specific lab threshold', 'New term added in v5.0', 'Grade description clarified'). Supports data managers and regulatory affairs teams in assessing the impact of CTCAE version upgrades on ongoing studies and in preparing regulatory submission change justifications.
reference: NCI CTCAE Version History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments; ALCOA+ Principles

description: Supplementary clinical criteria, laboratory thresholds, or objective measurement parameters that define the boundary conditions for assigning this specific grade to the AE term (e.g., specific lab value ranges, vital sign thresholds, functional impairment descriptors). Distinct from the grade_description in that it captures the measurable/objective criteria rather than the narrative description. Used by clinical staff for precise grade assignment and by biostatisticians for consistency validation.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CTCAE Grading Guidelines; ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM IG

description: The timestamp when this CTCAE grade reference record was first loaded into the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and GDPR Article 5 data integrity obligations. Used by data management teams to track when new CTCAE version data was ingested.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Term Code
description: Official NCI-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the CTCAE adverse event term within a given version. Used as the primary business identifier for cross-system referencing and CDISC SDTM mapping (AETOXGR domain). Enables unambiguous linkage between AE records and the reference grading criteria.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG v3.3 AE Domain; NCI Thesaurus (NCIt)

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version
description: Version number of the CTCAE publication from which this grade definition originates (e.g., 'v5.0', 'v4.03'). Critical for ensuring AE severity grading is applied against the correct version mandated by the study protocol. New CTCAE versions are released by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and may alter grade descriptions or add/remove terms.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on AE Reporting

description: The date on which this CTCAE grade definition was superseded, retired, or replaced by a newer version (nullable for currently active records). Used in conjunction with effective_start_date to implement bi-temporal versioning of the reference table, ensuring that AE records can always be validated against the grade criteria that were in effect at the time of the adverse event.
reference: NCI CTCAE Publication History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5 (data accuracy)

description: The date from which this CTCAE grade definition became effective and available for use in clinical trial AE grading (typically the official NCI publication date of the CTCAE version). Used to determine which version of a grade definition was applicable at the time of an AE occurrence, supporting retrospective audit and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: NCI CTCAE Publication History; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Numeric severity grade (1 through 5) as defined by CTCAE. Grade 1 = Mild; Grade 2 = Moderate; Grade 3 = Severe; Grade 4 = Life-threatening or disabling; Grade 5 = Death related to AE. This is the core grading dimension of the reference table and is used to populate the AETOXGR field in CDISC SDTM submissions and to trigger SAE/SUSAR reporting workflows in Oracle Argus Safety.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain

description: Full verbatim clinical description of the severity grade for the specific AE term as published in the CTCAE by NCI (e.g., for 'Nausea' Grade 2: 'Moderate nausea; oral intake decreased without significant weight loss, dehydration or malnutrition'). This is the authoritative clinical criteria text used by investigators and CRAs to assign the correct grade during AE assessment. Stored verbatim to preserve regulatory integrity.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+ Principles

description: Standardized textual label corresponding to the numeric CTCAE grade (e.g., 'Mild' for Grade 1, 'Moderate' for Grade 2, 'Severe' for Grade 3, 'Life-Threatening' for Grade 4, 'Death' for Grade 5). Provides a human-readable severity descriptor for use in clinical reports, DSMB/DMC safety narratives, and regulatory submissions without requiring a lookup of the numeric grade.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E2A; FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting

description: Additional clinical notes, caveats, or guidance provided by NCI for applying this specific grade to the AE term (e.g., 'Also consider Anemia', 'See also Cardiac disorders: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction'). Captures the 'Also consider' and 'Navigational Note' annotations present in the CTCAE publication that guide investigators in differential grading decisions.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on AE Assessment

description: Indicates whether this CTCAE grade definition record is currently active and available for use in new AE grading assignments. Set to False when a term or grade is retired, superseded by a newer CTCAE version, or deprecated. Enables version-controlled filtering so that active studies use only current, approved grading criteria while historical records remain accessible for audit.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether this CTCAE adverse event term and grade definition is specific to oncology/cancer treatment contexts. CTCAE was originally developed for oncology trials; some terms are exclusively relevant to chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy adverse effects. Used to filter applicable grading criteria for oncology versus non-oncology study protocols.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP); FDA Oncology Guidance

business_glossary_term: Serious Adverse Event (SAE) Flag by Grade
description: Indicates whether this CTCAE grade level is inherently classified as a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) based on regulatory definitions (typically Grade 3 and above may trigger SAE criteria, Grade 4–5 are always serious). Used to automate SAE flagging logic in Oracle Argus Safety and EDC systems (Medidata Rave) when a grade is recorded, supporting expedited reporting timelines under ICH E2A and FDA 21 CFR 312.32.
reference: ICH E2A Clinical Safety Data Management; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; NCI CTCAE v5.0

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code that most closely corresponds to this CTCAE adverse event term, enabling cross-coding between CTCAE and MedDRA terminologies. Used for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) that require MedDRA coding, and for signal detection in Oracle Argus Safety. Alignment maintained per current MedDRA version used in the study.
reference: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; MedDRA Introductory Guide; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain; FDA MedDRA Requirements

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) numeric code corresponding to the primary SOC classification of this CTCAE term's MedDRA PT cross-reference. Enables integrated safety tabulations that span both CTCAE-graded AE data and MedDRA-coded data in regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC reports.
reference: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Requirements

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used for the cross-reference mapping between this CTCAE term and its corresponding MedDRA PT/SOC codes (e.g., '26.0', '25.1'). MedDRA is updated biannually; version tracking ensures regulatory submissions reference the correct dictionary version as required by FDA, EMA, and PMDA.
reference: ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology; MedDRA Release Notes; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Requirements

business_glossary_term: National Cancer Institute (NCI) Thesaurus Concept ID
description: The NCI Thesaurus (NCIt) concept identifier (e.g., 'C54767') for this CTCAE adverse event term. Provides a stable, version-independent identifier from the NCI controlled vocabulary that persists across CTCAE versions. Used for ontology-based data integration, CDISC terminology alignment, and cross-study analytics in SAS Drug Development and AI/ML safety signal detection pipelines.
reference: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt); CDISC Controlled Terminology; NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The official publication date of the CTCAE version from which this grade definition originates, as released by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP). Provides the authoritative reference date for regulatory submissions and audit trails, distinct from the effective_start_date which may reflect internal adoption timing.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP); FDA Guidance on AE Reporting

description: The CTCAE term code from the immediately preceding CTCAE version that this record supersedes or corresponds to, enabling version-to-version lineage tracking. Used by data managers and biostatisticians to reconcile AE grading data collected under different CTCAE versions within the same study or across studies in integrated safety analyses.
reference: NCI CTCAE Version History; CDISC SDTM IG; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: The maximum number of calendar days within which an AE at this grade must be reported to regulatory authorities upon sponsor awareness (e.g., 7 days for fatal/life-threatening unexpected SUSARs, 15 days for other serious unexpected reactions, null for non-expedited grades). Drives automated due-date calculation in Oracle Argus Safety and regulatory_report_due_date population on the adverse_event product.
reference: FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI; EU CTR 536/2014; PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines

description: Indicates whether an AE recorded at this CTCAE grade level triggers mandatory expedited regulatory reporting obligations (e.g., 7-day or 15-day IND safety reports to FDA, EMA, PMDA). Derived from regulatory guidance but stored as a reference attribute to drive automated reporting workflow triggers in Oracle Argus Safety and CTMS. Supports compliance with FDA 21 CFR 312.32, EMA GVP Module VI, and ICH E2A timelines.
reference: FDA 21 CFR 312.32; ICH E2A; EMA GVP Module VI; PMDA Safety Reporting Guidelines; ICH E6(R2)

description: The two-letter CDISC SDTM domain code to which this CTCAE grade reference applies (e.g., 'AE' for Adverse Events domain). Supports SDTM dataset construction in SAS Drug Development and ensures correct domain-level mapping during regulatory submission preparation.
reference: CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

business_glossary_term: Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Variable Name
description: The CDISC SDTM variable name to which this CTCAE grade value maps in regulatory submission datasets (e.g., 'AETOXGR' for the AE domain toxicity grade). Used by SAS Drug Development programmers and CDISC data managers to ensure correct SDTM dataset population and FDA/EMA submission compliance.
reference: CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide AE Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

description: NCI-assigned code for the System Organ Class (SOC) category within the CTCAE hierarchy. Enables programmatic grouping and filtering of adverse event terms by organ system for safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC reports, and regulatory submissions. Distinct from MedDRA SOC codes but may be cross-referenced.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; NCI Thesaurus (NCIt); CDISC SDTM IG AE Domain

description: The System Organ Class (SOC) category name as defined in the CTCAE, representing the highest-level anatomical or physiological grouping of adverse event terms (e.g., 'Cardiac disorders', 'Gastrointestinal disorders', 'Nervous system disorders'). Aligns with MedDRA SOC hierarchy for cross-coding purposes. Used for safety signal detection and aggregate reporting by organ system.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH M1 MedDRA Terminology

description: Reference to the specific section, page, or table in the official NCI CTCAE publication document from which this grade definition was extracted (e.g., 'CTCAE v5.0, Section 2, Table: Cardiac Disorders, p.12'). Supports regulatory inspection readiness and audit trail requirements by providing a direct link to the authoritative source document stored in Veeva Vault eTMF.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

value_regex: Oracle Argus Safety|SAS Drug Development|NCI CTCAE|Manual
description: The operational system or authoritative source from which this CTCAE grade reference record was loaded (e.g., 'Oracle Argus Safety' where CTCAE codes are maintained, 'SAS Drug Development' for CDISC-aligned reference data, 'NCI CTCAE' for direct NCI publication ingestion). Supports data lineage tracking and Silver layer provenance requirements.
reference: ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC Data Management Standards

description: The timestamp of the most recent update to this CTCAE grade reference record in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks corrections, enrichments, or metadata updates applied after initial load. Required for audit trail completeness under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

description: The document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF for the official NCI CTCAE source document associated with this version. Enables direct navigation from the reference record to the controlled source document in the electronic Trial Master File, supporting audit trail completeness and regulatory inspection readiness per 21 CFR Part 11 and EU CTR 536/2014.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF System

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each MedDRA term record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key. [REFERENCE_LOOKUP role — _canonical_skip_reason: This entity is a standardized regulatory reference code list (MedDRA hierarchy) maintained by MSSO/ICH; per-role minimums for REFERENCE_LOOKUP are exempt.]
reference: MedDRA Maintenance and Support Services Organization (MSSO); ICH M1 Guideline

business_glossary_term: Oracle Argus Safety Dictionary Record ID
description: The internal dictionary record identifier assigned by Oracle Argus Safety when this MedDRA term is loaded into the Argus dictionary module. Enables direct cross-reference between the lakehouse silver layer and the Oracle Argus Safety system of record for adverse event coding reconciliation and audit.
reference: Oracle Argus Safety Dictionary Management Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Describes the nature of the change applied to this term in the current MedDRA version: 'new' (first introduced), 'modified' (name or hierarchy changed), 'retired' (removed from active use), 'split' (one term divided into multiple), 'merged' (multiple terms combined), or 'reinstated' (previously retired term reactivated). Critical for managing dictionary upgrade impacts in Oracle Argus Safety.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Change Documentation; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: The timestamp when this MedDRA term record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles for the clinical data management platform.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade Mapping
description: The CTCAE v5.0 term name that corresponds to this MedDRA PT, where a direct mapping exists. Enables cross-referencing between MedDRA coding and CTCAE severity grading used in oncology and other therapeutic area studies. Null where no CTCAE mapping exists for this term.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; MedDRA-CTCAE Mapping Table; CDISC SDTM IG; FDA Oncology Guidance

description: The date from which this MedDRA term is officially effective and available for use in adverse event coding and regulatory submissions, corresponding to the MSSO release date of the version in which it was introduced. Supports version-gating logic in Oracle Argus Safety and study-level coding version controls.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: The level within the five-tier MedDRA hierarchy to which this term belongs: LLT (Lowest Level Term), PT (Preferred Term), HLT (High Level Term), HLGT (High Level Group Term), or SOC (System Organ Class). Determines how the term is used in adverse event coding, CTCAE mapping, and regulatory aggregate reporting.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD, AEBODSYS); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the High Level Group Term (HLGT) in the primary SOC path for this term. Populated for LLT, PT, HLT, and HLGT level terms to support aggregate safety analysis and regulatory tabulations at the HLGT level.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The official MedDRA name of the High Level Group Term (HLGT) in the primary SOC path. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations and signal detection analytics without requiring a hierarchy traversal.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the High Level Term (HLT) in the primary SOC path for this term. Populated for LLT, PT, and HLT level terms to support aggregate safety analysis at the HLT level in regulatory submissions and DSMB/DMC reports.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The official MedDRA name of the High Level Term (HLT) in the primary SOC path. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations and signal detection analytics.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The MedDRA version in which this term was first introduced into the dictionary. Supports historical analysis of term availability across study timelines and ensures correct version-gating when coding adverse events from legacy studies.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term History Documentation

description: Applicable to LLT-level terms only. Indicates whether the LLT is a 'current' LLT (true) — meaning it maps to a PT with the same name — or a 'non-current' LLT (false) that maps to a PT with a different name. Current LLTs are preferred for new coding; non-current LLTs are retained for historical traceability per MSSO policy.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO LLT Currency Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

description: Indicates whether this term's association to a System Organ Class (SOC) is the primary (true) or secondary (false) SOC linkage. MedDRA allows a PT to be linked to multiple SOCs; the primary SOC is used for regulatory aggregate safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC safety reviews, and CTCAE-aligned reporting.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEBODSYS); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: ISO 639-1/639-2 language code for the language of this term record (e.g., 'en' for English, 'ja' for Japanese, 'de' for German). MedDRA is published in multiple languages; this field supports multi-language implementations required for submissions to PMDA (Japanese), EMA (EU languages), and Health Canada (French/English).
reference: ISO 639-1; MedDRA Multi-Language Guide; PMDA Submission Requirements; EMA MedDRA Policy; Health Canada Guidance

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_code. For higher-level terms this field is null. LLTs capture verbatim-level medical concepts and are the entry point for verbatim-to-MedDRA coding in Oracle Argus Safety and EDC systems.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG; FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: The official MedDRA name of the Lowest Level Term (LLT). For LLT-level records this equals term_name. Null for higher-level terms. Used in verbatim coding workflows and auto-coding dictionaries in Oracle Argus Safety.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG

description: The date on which this MedDRA term record was loaded into the lakehouse silver layer from the MSSO distribution files. Used to track the effective date of each biannual dictionary update and to support audit trails required under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The biannual MedDRA release version in which this term was introduced or last updated (e.g., '27.0', '26.1'). Critical for regulatory submissions requiring version-specific coding, database lock (DBL) documentation, and CDISC SDTM dataset compliance. MedDRA releases occur twice yearly (March and September).
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Release Schedule; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. For PT-level records this equals term_code. For LLT-level records this is the parent PT code. Used as the primary coding level in Oracle Argus Safety adverse event records, CDISC SDTM (AEDECOD), and regulatory case submissions (ICH E2B).
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD); FDA Adverse Event Reporting; EMA MedDRA Policy

description: The official MedDRA name of the Preferred Term (PT) to which this term maps. Denormalized for direct use in adverse event coding displays, safety narratives, CDISC SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions without requiring a hierarchy join.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM IG (AEDECOD); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

business_glossary_term: Medidata Rave EDC Dictionary Entry ID
description: The dictionary entry identifier assigned by Medidata Rave EDC when this MedDRA term is configured in the Rave coding dictionary for eCRF verbatim-to-MedDRA auto-coding. Supports reconciliation between EDC-coded adverse events and the master MedDRA reference in the lakehouse.
reference: Medidata Rave Coding Module Documentation; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC SDTM IG

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code of the term that replaces this term when it has been retired, split, or merged. Null for active terms and retired terms with no direct replacement. Supports automated re-coding workflows in Oracle Argus Safety during biannual MedDRA version upgrades.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement and Replacement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

description: The MedDRA version in which this term was retired, if applicable. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding rules in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms that should not be applied to new adverse event records after the specified version.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

description: The date on which this MedDRA term was officially retired by MSSO, corresponding to the release date of the version in which it was retired. Null for active terms. Used to enforce coding restrictions in Oracle Argus Safety and to flag terms in legacy study datasets.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

description: Pipe-delimited list of Standardised MedDRA Query (SMQ) names to which this PT belongs. SMQs are validated, topic-focused groupings of MedDRA terms used for signal detection, aggregate safety analysis, and regulatory queries (e.g., 'Anaphylactic reaction', 'Drug-induced liver injury'). Populated for PT-level terms only.
reference: MedDRA SMQ Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SMQ Documentation; ICH E2B(R3); EMA Signal Detection Guidance

description: Indicates whether this term's SMQ membership is classified as 'broad' (higher sensitivity, more inclusive) or 'narrow' (higher specificity, more restrictive) within the associated SMQ. Used to configure signal detection algorithms in Oracle Argus Safety and to define the scope of safety queries in regulatory submissions.
reference: MedDRA SMQ Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SMQ Documentation; EMA Signal Detection Guidance; ICH E2B(R3)

description: The standardized two-to-four letter abbreviation for the System Organ Class (SOC) as defined by MSSO (e.g., 'CARD' for Cardiac disorders, 'NERV' for Nervous system disorders). Used in safety tabulation headers, DSMB/DMC slide decks, and abbreviated regulatory reports.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO SOC Abbreviation List; ICH M1

description: The 8-digit MedDRA code for the System Organ Class (SOC) to which this term is linked (primary or secondary). Populated for all hierarchy levels to enable direct SOC-level filtering in safety tabulations, signal detection, and regulatory submissions without requiring a hierarchy traversal join.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1; CDISC SDTM IG (AEBODSYS); EMA MedDRA Policy

description: The official MedDRA name of the System Organ Class (SOC) associated with this term. Denormalized for direct use in safety tabulations, DSMB/DMC reports, and CDISC SDTM datasets (AEBODSYS variable) without requiring a hierarchy join.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; CDISC SDTM IG; ICH E2B(R3); FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: The name of the MSSO-distributed MedDRA ASCII flat file from which this term record was loaded (e.g., 'llt.asc', 'pt.asc', 'hlt.asc', 'hlgt.asc', 'soc.asc'). Supports data lineage traceability and ETL audit for the biannual MedDRA dictionary update process in the Databricks lakehouse.
reference: MSSO MedDRA Distribution File Format Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

description: The official 8-digit numeric MedDRA term code assigned by the Maintenance and Support Services Organization (MSSO) uniquely identifying this term within the MedDRA hierarchy. Used as the primary lookup key in Oracle Argus Safety for adverse event coding and regulatory submissions.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; FDA MedDRA Requirements; EMA MedDRA Policy

description: The official MedDRA term label as published by MSSO for this term code. Represents the standardized medical concept name used in adverse event coding, regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA), and safety signal detection across all five hierarchy levels.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; ICH M1 Guideline; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

description: Indicates whether the MedDRA term is currently active and available for coding or has been retired in a subsequent MedDRA version release. Retired terms are retained for historical traceability of previously coded adverse events but must not be used for new coding in Oracle Argus Safety.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Retirement Policy; ICH E2B(R3) Guideline

description: Classifies the term as 'standard' (fully endorsed MedDRA term) or 'non-standard' (a term that has been superseded, split, or merged and retained for backward compatibility). Drives coding validation rules in Oracle Argus Safety and Medidata Rave auto-coding configurations.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide v27.0; MSSO Term Classification Policy; ICH E2B(R3)

description: The timestamp when this MedDRA term record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer, typically triggered by a biannual MedDRA version release load. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: The corresponding WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology (WHO-ART) preferred term code or name for this MedDRA term, where a legacy mapping exists. Supports legacy study migration and cross-dictionary reconciliation for studies coded under WHO-ART prior to MedDRA adoption.
reference: WHO-ART to MedDRA Mapping Guide; MSSO Cross-Dictionary Mapping; ICH M1

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the safety narrative record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this data product.

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this safety narrative was generated.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM; FDA IND regulations

description: Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) associated with this safety narrative. Links to the subject master record.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM DM domain

description: Date on which the adverse event first began, as reported by the investigator or subject. Critical for calculating reporting timelines and for CDISC SDTM AE domain mapping.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.3; CDISC SDTM AE.AESTDTC; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: Coded outcome of the adverse event at the time of narrative authoring or case closure. Aligns with ICH E2B(R3) outcome codes and CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT controlled terminology.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.8; CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT; FDA MedWatch 3500A

description: Date on which the adverse event resolved or stabilized. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of narrative authoring. Used to determine event duration and outcome status.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.8; CDISC SDTM AE.AEENDTC; ICH E2A

description: Date on which the medical monitor formally approved the final version of the safety narrative for regulatory submission. Represents the final lifecycle milestone before submission.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; Oracle Argus Safety

description: The externally-known case number assigned by Oracle Argus Safety to the adverse event case. Used as the primary business identifier for cross-system traceability and regulatory submissions.
reference: Oracle Argus Safety; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch

description: Date on which the safety narrative was initially authored or drafted. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and version history tracking.
reference: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Argus Safety

description: High-level executive summary of the safety case, synthesizing the patient description, event, treatment, and outcome into a concise paragraph suitable for inclusion in the ICSR narrative field of E2B(R3) submissions.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) Section H.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Classification of the safety case for which this narrative is written. SAE = Serious Adverse Event; SUSAR = Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction; AE = Adverse Event; AESI = Adverse Event of Special Interest.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Medical monitor's or investigator's assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse event. Used in regulatory reporting and signal detection.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2.r.4; WHO-UMC causality categories; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Timestamp when this safety narrative record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements.
reference: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) severity grade assigned to the adverse event (1=Mild, 2=Moderate, 3=Severe, 4=Life-threatening, 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection and regulatory reporting.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AE.AETOXGR; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

description: Version of the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events used for severity grading in this narrative (e.g., '5.0'). Ensures consistency in grading across study sites and regulatory submissions.
reference: NCI CTCAE; CDISC SDTM; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Review Date
description: Date on which the DSMB or DMC reviewed this safety case. Populated only when dsmb_reviewed is True. Used to track safety oversight compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees

business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reviewed Flag
description: Indicates whether this safety case and its narrative have been reviewed by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC). True if reviewed; False if not yet presented to the DSMB/DMC.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees; EMA Reflection Paper on DMCs

description: Unique message identifier assigned to the ICSR transmission in E2B(R3) XML format as submitted via eCTD to health authorities. Enables traceability between the narrative record and the regulatory submission artifact.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway; EMA EVWEB; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Detailed narrative describing the onset, nature, severity, and clinical course of the adverse event or serious adverse event, including signs, symptoms, and diagnostic findings. Core narrative section for ICSR submissions.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) Section C.2; ICH E2A; FDA MedWatch 3500A; EMA GVP Module VI

reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ Principles; Oracle Argus Safety

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Severity Grade
description: The CTCAE severity grade assigned to the SAE, ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Grade 3 = severe, Grade 4 = life-threatening, Grade 5 = death. Used for oncology and other therapeutic area safety assessments.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; CDISC SDTM AE.AETOXGR; FDA Guidance on Adverse Event Reporting

business_glossary_term: Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Reported Flag
description: Indicates whether this SAE was reported to the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) for independent safety review. Required for studies with an active DSMB/DMC charter.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006); EMA Reflection Paper on DMCs

description: Indicates whether the SAE is expected (listed in the Investigator's Brochure or product labeling) or unexpected (not listed or differing in nature/severity). Unexpected + serious + related = SUSAR, triggering expedited regulatory reporting.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

description: Sequential number indicating which follow-up report this record represents (0 = initial report, 1 = first follow-up, 2 = second follow-up, etc.). Used to track the evolution of the SAE case over time as new information becomes available.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3); Oracle Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: The date on which the SAE was first reported to the sponsor or CRO by the investigational site. This is Day 0 for calculating regulatory reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting clock).
reference: ICH E2A Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EMA GVP Module VI; Oracle Argus Safety

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Notification Date
description: The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of the SAE. Required under GCP and local regulations to ensure ongoing ethical oversight of the study.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.3; 21 CFR Part 312.66; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
description: Indicates whether this SAE has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting to health authorities (e.g., FDA 7/15-day reporting, EMA reporting). Derived from causality, expectedness, and seriousness criteria but stored as a business flag.
reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI

description: The MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) code that most closely matches the verbatim SAE term. The LLT is the most granular level of MedDRA coding and is used to preserve the original reported term in a coded format.
reference: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AELLT

description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code assigned to the SAE. The PT is the primary level of MedDRA used for regulatory reporting and is the standard coded term submitted in ICSRs and clinical study reports.
reference: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AEDECOD; ICH E2B(R3)

description: The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code assigned to the SAE during medical coding. Represents the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy, used for regulatory submissions and safety signal detection.
reference: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM AE.AESOC

description: The version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this SAE (e.g., '26.0', '26.1'). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding and compliance with current dictionary standards.
reference: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; ICH E2B(R3); CDISC SDTM

description: The full medical narrative describing the SAE, including clinical course, relevant medical history, concomitant medications, investigational product details, and the investigator's assessment. This is the primary free-text field in the Argus Safety case and is included in regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E2A Section 6; ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 312.32; Oracle Argus Safety

description: The date on which the serious adverse event first began or was first observed by the subject or investigator. This is the principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for the SAE transaction.
reference: ICH E2A Section 3; CDISC SDTM AE.AESTDTC; 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: The clinical outcome of the serious adverse event at the time of the most recent report. 'recovered_with_sequelae' indicates the subject recovered but with lasting effects. 'fatal' must align with seriousness_death = true.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) Element C.1.7; CDISC SDTM AE.AEOUT; Oracle Argus Safety

description: The calculated deadline by which the expedited regulatory report (e.g., IND Safety Report, SUSAR notification) must be submitted to the relevant health authority. Typically 7 calendar days for fatal/life-threatening SUSARs and 15 calendar days for other SUSARs.
reference: ICH E2A Section 5; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 42; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Classifies the type of safety report generated for this SAE. 'expedited' = 7/15-day SUSAR or IND safety report; 'periodic' = included in DSUR/PSUR; 'spontaneous' = post-marketing spontaneous report; 'literature' = identified from published literature.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2C(R2) DSUR; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: The health authority or regulatory body to which the SAE/SUSAR report was submitted (e.g., 'FDA', 'EMA', 'MHRA', 'PMDA', 'TGA', 'Health Canada'). reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA GVP Module VI; MHRA; PMDA

description: The date on which the serious adverse event resolved, stabilized, or the subject died. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of reporting.

description: Current lifecycle status of the SAE case in Oracle Argus Safety. 'initial' = first report received; 'follow_up' = additional information received; 'closed' = case fully resolved and closed; 'nullified' = case determined not to meet SAE criteria and voided.

description: The verbatim (as-reported) description of the serious adverse event as recorded by the investigator or site staff in the source document or eCRF. This is the raw, uncoded term prior to MedDRA coding.

business_glossary_term: Seriousness Criterion: Congenital Anomaly or Birth Defect

description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in death of the subject. One of the six ICH E2A seriousness criteria that must be captured individually.
reference: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in persistent or significant disability or incapacity.
reference: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of requiring inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization.
reference: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being immediately life-threatening (i.e., the subject was at immediate risk of death at the time of the event).
reference: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

business_glossary_term: Seriousness Criterion: Other Medically Important Condition
description: Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being an other medically important condition — events that may not be immediately life-threatening but may jeopardize the subject or require intervention to prevent one of the other serious outcomes.
reference: ICH E2A Section 2; 21 CFR Part 312.32(a); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Reference identifier for the source document (e.g., hospital discharge summary, death certificate, medical records) that supports the SAE report. Used for SDV and audit trail purposes per ALCOA+ principles.

reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Indicates whether this product record represents a comparator (active control or placebo) rather than the primary investigational product (True = comparator). Enables differentiation of IMP vs. comparator in supply chain, SDTM, and safety reporting.
reference: ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Indicates whether this product record represents a placebo (True) rather than an active investigational product or comparator. Used in RTSM randomization configuration, supply chain, and SDTM EX domain coding.
reference: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Name of the pharmaceutical manufacturer or contract manufacturing organization (CMO) responsible for producing the investigational product. Referenced in the IMPD/IND CMC section and supply chain records in SAP S/4HANA.
reference: ICH Q7 GMP; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; EMA GMP Guidelines; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Physical site or facility name and location where the investigational product is manufactured. Required for regulatory submissions (IND/IMPD) and GMP compliance tracking. Distinct from the manufacturer legal entity name.
reference: ICH Q7 GMP; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; EMA GMP Guidelines

description: Pharmacological mechanism by which the investigational product exerts its therapeutic effect (e.g., selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor). Captured in the IND/IMPD and referenced in the protocol background section.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA IND Guidance; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) number for the investigational product, if applicable. Used for US regulatory submissions, pharmacy dispensing records, and drug accountability tracking. May be absent for novel compounds not yet assigned an NDC.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 207; FDA NDC Directory

description: Free-text operational notes or comments regarding the investigational product record, such as special handling instructions, known stability issues, or interim regulatory communications. Captured by data management or regulatory affairs teams.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Description of the primary and secondary packaging configuration for the investigational product (e.g., 'blister pack of 10 tablets in a carton', 'single-use vial 10 mL in a kit'). Referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and RTSM kit configuration.
reference: ICH Q8; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.94; EMA IMPD Guideline; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Classification of the investigational product by modality type (e.g., small molecule, biologic, gene therapy, medical device). Drives regulatory pathway selection, storage requirements, and supply chain handling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|gene_therapy|cell_therapy|medical_device|combination_product|vaccine|radiopharmaceutical — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA 21 CFR Parts 312/812; EMA Guideline on IMP; ICH Q6A/Q6B

description: Current regulatory approval status of the investigational product (e.g., approved for a different indication, purely investigational, withdrawn from market). Informs regulatory strategy, labeling requirements, and comparator sourcing decisions.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E6(R2)

description: Period in months after which the investigational product must be retested before continued use, applicable to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and certain formulations. Distinct from shelf life; used in supply chain and QC planning.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Route by which the investigational product is administered to subjects (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Captured per CDISC SDTM EX domain EXROUTE variable and referenced in protocol and pharmacy instructions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|intrathecal — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain (EXROUTE); FDA Route of Administration Terminology; ICH M5

description: Approved shelf life of the investigational product in months from the date of manufacture, as established by stability studies and documented in the IMPD/IND. Drives expiry date calculation, supply planning, and resupply triggers in Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Sponsor's internal product or compound code used in portfolio management systems, distinct from the IMP code used in clinical operations. Enables cross-referencing between clinical development and commercial product pipelines.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Sponsor SOPs; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Required storage conditions for the investigational product as specified in the IMPD/IND and product label (e.g., 'Store at 2–8°C, protected from light', 'Store below 25°C'). Critical for supply chain cold chain management and site pharmacy compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Maximum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

description: Minimum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

description: Nominal strength or concentration of the active substance in the investigational product as labeled (e.g., '10 mg', '100 mg/mL', '5 mg/kg'). Captured in the IMPD/IND and referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and SDTM EX domain.
reference: ICH Q6A; CDISC SDTM EX Domain (EXDOSE); FDA CMC Guidance

description: Unit of measure for the investigational product strength (e.g., mg, mg/mL, IU). Standardized per CDISC controlled terminology to enable cross-study comparisons and SDTM dataset generation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg|mg/mL|mg/kg|mcg|mcg/mL|IU|IU/mL|g|% — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology (UNIT); ICH Q6A; FDA CMC Guidance

description: Therapeutic or pharmacological class of the investigational product (e.g., oncology, cardiovascular, CNS, anti-infective). Used for portfolio analytics, regulatory strategy, and study feasibility assessments.
reference: WHO ATC; MedDRA SOC; FDA Pharmacologic Class

description: The unit in which the investigational product is dispensed to subjects at the investigational site (e.g., tablet, vial, kit, syringe). Used in RTSM dispensing records, drug accountability logs, and SDTM EX domain. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tablet|capsule|vial|kit|syringe|patch|sachet|bottle|ampoule — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2)

description: Timestamp when the investigational product master record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and change management tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) drug code assigned to the investigational product for standardized drug coding in adverse event reporting, SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions. Enables cross-study signal detection in Oracle Argus Safety.
reference: WHO-DD; CDISC SDTM CM/EX domains; ICH E2B(R3)

business_glossary_term: Ip Site Accountability - Ip Site Accountability Id
description: Primary key for the ip_site_accountability association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Ip Site Accountability - Investigational Product Id
description: Foreign key linking to the investigational product master record for which site-level accountability is being tracked.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Ip Site Accountability - Investigational Site Id
description: Foreign key linking to the investigational site at which the IMP is stored, dispensed, and accounted for.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Reference identifier linking to the drug accountability log maintained at the site for this IMP. Required by GCP to reconcile quantities received, dispensed, returned, and destroyed.
Overall lifecycle status of this IMP-site accountability record, reflecting whether the site is currently active for this product across both storage and dispensing dimensions.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Current authorization status for the site to dispense this investigational product to trial subjects. Distinct from storage authorization — a site may store but not yet be authorized to dispense.
Date on which the investigational site was formally authorized to store this investigational product. Belongs to the IMP-site relationship, not to either master record alone.
reference: 21 CFR 312.62, ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Current GCP storage compliance status for this IMP at this specific site. Reflects whether the site is meeting required storage conditions (e.g., temperature range) for this product.

Cumulative count of documented temperature excursions recorded for this IMP at this site. Belongs to the IMP-site relationship as it reflects the storage history of a specific product at a specific location.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2), 21 CFR 211.68

description: Primary key for the product_designation association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product that holds this special regulatory designation.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the special regulatory designation record granted to this investigational product.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The clinical development phase of the investigational product at the time this designation was granted or at which the designation is applicable. Belongs to the association because the same product may receive different designations at different development phases. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: ICH E8 development phase classification

description: Classification of the special regulatory designation as it applies to this specific investigational product pairing. Sourced from detection phase relationship data. Captures which type of expedited pathway applies in this product-designation context.
reference: FDA/EMA designation classification taxonomy

description: Calendar date on which the health authority officially granted this specific designation to this specific investigational product. Belongs to the association because the same product may receive the same designation type at different dates for different indications. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.

The specific disease, condition, or patient population for which this designation applies to this investigational product. Belongs to the association because the same product may hold different designations for different indications, and the same designation type may cover different indication scopes across products. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: ICD-10 / MedDRA indication coding

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each study arm record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for the study_arm data product.
reference: CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: FK to study.investigational_product
Reference to the parent clinical study to which this arm belongs. Links the arm to its governing study protocol.
reference: CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether this arm is part of an adaptive trial design where arm allocation, sample size, or continuation may be modified based on interim analysis results per a pre-specified adaptation rule.
reference: FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs (2019); EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs; ICH E9(R1)

description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the arm within the study. Maps directly to the ARMCD variable in the CDISC SDTM ARM domain and is used in randomization and data tabulation.
reference: CDISC SDTM v3.3 ARM Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology

description: Full descriptive name of the study arm as defined in the protocol (e.g., 'Drug A 10mg QD', 'Placebo'). Maps to the ARM variable in the CDISC SDTM ARM domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM v3.3 ARM Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6

description: Current lifecycle status of the study arm, reflecting whether the arm is planned, actively enrolling, suspended, closed to enrollment, or discontinued per protocol amendment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Classification of the arm per ClinicalTrials.gov and CDISC controlled terminology, indicating the nature of the intervention assigned to subjects in this arm. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Experimental|Active Comparator|Placebo Comparator|Sham Comparator|No Intervention|Other — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
reference: ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; CDISC SDTM Controlled Terminology; ICH E8(R1)

description: Specifies the level of blinding applied to this arm: Open Label (no blinding), Single Blind (subject blinded), Double Blind (subject and investigator blinded), or Triple Blind (subject, investigator, and sponsor blinded).
reference: ICH E9(R1); ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain

description: The native arm identifier assigned by Oracle Clinical One (the source system of record for study design and patient randomization). Used for system-of-record traceability and data lineage from source to lakehouse.
reference: Oracle Clinical One Study Design Module; ALCOA+ Principles

description: The date and time when this study arm record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Arm Reference
description: The arm reference identifier as recorded in Oracle Siebel CTMS for site monitoring, visit tracking, and enrollment management. Supports cross-system reconciliation.
reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reason for early discontinuation of the study arm, if applicable (e.g., safety signal, futility, sponsor decision, regulatory hold). Required for regulatory reporting when an arm is terminated prior to planned completion.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

description: Textual description of the dose level and regimen for the investigational product in this arm (e.g., '10 mg once daily', '200 mg BID'). Supports dose-response analysis and protocol compliance monitoring.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6.4; CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Frequency of investigational product administration for subjects in this arm (e.g., QD - once daily, BID - twice daily, QW - once weekly). Aligns with CDISC SDTM EX domain EXDOSFRQ variable.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The date on which the study arm was closed to enrollment or treatment, either per protocol schedule or due to early termination. Null if the arm is still active.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU CTR 536/2014; Oracle Clinical One

description: Indicates whether this arm is subject to one or more pre-specified interim analyses by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) during the study.
reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter Requirements

description: Detailed narrative description of the intervention assigned to subjects in this arm, including drug name, dose, route of administration, and dosing schedule as specified in the study protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6.4; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Category of the therapeutic intervention assigned to subjects in this arm. Aligns with ClinicalTrials.gov intervention type classifications and supports regulatory submission categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Drug|Biologic|Device|Procedure|Behavioral|Dietary Supplement|Radiation|Genetic|Combination|Other — promote to reference product]
reference: ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014

description: Indicates whether the treatment assignment for this arm is blinded to subjects, investigators, or both (double-blind). Supports blinding integrity tracking and unblinding event management.
reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.7; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Indicates whether this arm serves as the control arm (comparator) in the study design. True for placebo, active comparator, or sham comparator arms used as the reference group in statistical analyses.
reference: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1); CDISC SDTM ARM Domain

description: Indicates whether subjects enrolled in this arm are included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population as defined in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP).
reference: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM ADSL; FDA Statistical Guidance

description: The maximum allowable number of subjects that may be enrolled in this arm, including any over-enrollment buffer defined in the protocol. Distinct from planned_subjects_count which reflects the statistical target.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6.7; Oracle Clinical One; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: The minimum number of subjects required in this arm to maintain statistical validity of the study, as defined in the SAP. Used for futility analysis and early stopping rule evaluation.
reference: ICH E9(R1); SAP Requirements; FDA Statistical Guidance

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, clarifications, or protocol-specific instructions related to this arm that are not captured in structured fields. For internal use by study team.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Clinical One

description: The planned (target) number of subjects to be enrolled and randomized into this arm as specified in the study protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP).
reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6.7; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain

description: Indicates whether subjects enrolled in this arm are included in the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population as defined in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP). Subjects with major protocol deviations may be excluded.
reference: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM ADSL; FDA Statistical Guidance

description: The version identifier of the study protocol or protocol amendment under which this arm was defined or last modified. Ensures traceability of arm design to the governing protocol document.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain

description: The allocation ratio for randomization of subjects into this arm relative to other arms (e.g., '1:1', '2:1:1'). Used by the RTSM/IRT system (Medidata Rave RTSM) to control subject assignment.
reference: ICH E9(R1); CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Numeric representation of the allocation weight for this arm relative to total allocation (e.g., 0.50 for a 1:1 ratio arm). Supports quantitative analysis and reporting of enrollment balance.
reference: ICH E9(R1); CDISC SDTM ARM Domain

description: The route by which the investigational product is administered to subjects in this arm (e.g., Oral, Intravenous, Subcutaneous, Intramuscular). Aligns with CDISC SDTM EX domain EXROUTE variable and WHO-DD terminology.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; WHO-DD; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; NCI Thesaurus

description: Indicates whether subjects enrolled in this arm are included in the safety analysis population (all subjects who received at least one dose of study treatment), as defined in the SAP.
reference: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM ADSL; FDA Statistical Guidance; ICH E6(R2) GCP

business_glossary_term: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Arm Domain
description: CDISC SDTM domain identifier confirming this arm maps to the ARM domain in the SDTM submission dataset. Always 'ARM' per CDISC standard; included for regulatory submission traceability.
reference: CDISC SDTM v3.3 ARM Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA CDISC Requirements

description: Ordinal sequence number defining the display and processing order of arms within the study. Used for consistent ordering in reports, eCRFs, and SDTM datasets.
reference: CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; Oracle Clinical One Study Design

description: The date on which the study arm became active and eligible for subject enrollment, as defined in the approved protocol or protocol amendment. Supports enrollment timeline tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU CTR 536/2014; Oracle Clinical One

description: Planned duration of treatment for subjects in this arm, expressed in days. Used for supply planning, visit schedule design, and protocol compliance monitoring.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6.4; CDISC SDTM ARM Domain; Oracle Clinical One

description: The username or system identifier of the user or process that last modified this study arm record. Required for audit trail compliance under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable) principle.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

description: The date and time when this study arm record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

description: The username or system identifier of the user or process that created this study arm record. Required for audit trail compliance under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable) principle.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each eligibility criterion record in the clinical study. Primary key for the eligibility_criterion data product.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Foreign key linking to safety.meddra_term. Business justification: eligibility_criterion has meddra_pt_code and meddra_pt_name as plain attributes — inclusion/exclusion criteria referencing medical conditions are MedDRA-coded for SDTM IE domain mapping and regulatory
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the prior version of this criterion that was superseded by the current record. Enables full version history chain for audit trail and regulatory traceability of criterion evolution across protocol amendments.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which this criterion was introduced or last modified. Supports amendment-driven criterion tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM IE Domain

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this eligibility criterion is defined. Links the criterion to its parent study protocol.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: eligibility_criterion has amendment_number as a STRING and is_amendment_driven BOOLEAN flag but no FK to study_protocol_amendment. Eligibility criteria are frequently introduced or modified by protoco
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Specifies the sub-population to which this criterion applies when it is not universally applicable to all subjects (e.g., reproductive status criteria apply to FEMALE_ONLY, pediatric dosing criteria apply to PEDIATRIC). Supports conditional screening logic.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ICH E11 (Pediatric Studies); FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: The documented scientific or operational rationale for introducing or modifying this criterion, particularly when driven by a protocol amendment. Required for regulatory submissions and IRB/IEC amendment packages.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The date and time when this eligibility criterion record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: The page or section reference in the electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) where this eligibility criterion is assessed and documented. Used for site training, monitoring, and Source Data Verification (SDV) activities.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave EDC

description: Clinical or operational category classifying the nature of the criterion. Supports structured analysis and site training. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DEMOGRAPHIC|DIAGNOSIS|LAB_VALUE|PRIOR_THERAPY|CONCOMITANT_MEDICATION|REPRODUCTIVE_STATUS|WASHOUT_PERIOD|CONSENT|OTHER — promote to reference product]
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain (IESCAT); ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Sequential number assigned to the criterion within its type (inclusion or exclusion) as it appears in the study protocol. Used for ordering and referencing in site screening checklists and EDC eligibility modules.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain (IESEQ); ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Abbreviated or condensed label for the criterion used in EDC display, site training materials, and operational screening tools where full text is impractical. Maps to CDISC SDTM IE domain variable IETESTCD.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain (IETESTCD); ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Current lifecycle status of the eligibility criterion. DRAFT indicates under review; ACTIVE indicates approved and in use; SUPERSEDED indicates replaced by an amended version; RETIRED indicates removed from the protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Full verbatim text of the eligibility criterion as written in the approved study protocol. This is the authoritative, protocol-exact wording used in site screening checklists, EDC eligibility modules, and regulatory submissions. Maps to CDISC SDTM IE domain variable IETEST.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain (IETEST); ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether the criterion is an inclusion criterion (subject must meet) or an exclusion criterion (subject must not meet) for enrollment eligibility. Maps to CDISC SDTM IE domain variable IECAT.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain (IECAT); ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The display sequence order for this criterion within its type group (inclusion or exclusion) as it should appear in site screening checklists, EDC eligibility modules, and protocol documents. May differ from criterion_number when criteria are reordered by amendment.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

business_glossary_term: Electronic Data Capture (EDC) Field Object Identifier (OID)
description: The Object Identifier (OID) of the corresponding field in the Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system (e.g., Medidata Rave) eligibility module. Enables direct mapping between the protocol criterion and the EDC data collection form for data lineage and validation.
reference: CDISC ODM (Operational Data Model); Medidata Rave EDC; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The date from which this criterion version became operationally effective for subject screening. Aligns with the IRB/IEC approval date of the applicable protocol version.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46; EU CTR 536/2014

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) Approval Required Flag
description: Indicates whether a change to this criterion requires formal IRB/IEC approval before implementation at sites. Typically True for all criteria changes driven by protocol amendments.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR Part 56

description: Indicates whether this criterion was introduced or modified as a result of a protocol amendment. True when the criterion originated from or was changed by a formal protocol amendment. Critical for regulatory audit trails and amendment impact analysis.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether this criterion is designated as critical, meaning a violation would constitute a major protocol deviation requiring immediate reporting to the sponsor and potentially the IRB/IEC. Critical criteria are typically safety-related or have significant impact on data integrity.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM IE Domain

description: The standardized laboratory test code (e.g., LOINC code or sponsor-defined code) for the lab parameter referenced in this criterion. Applicable for lab value criteria such as eGFR, hemoglobin, or platelet count thresholds.
reference: LOINC; CDISC SDTM LB Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
description: The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code associated with the diagnosis, condition, or medical history referenced in this criterion. Enables standardized medical coding for regulatory submissions and cross-study analysis.
reference: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities); ICH M1; CDISC SDTM

description: The date and time when this eligibility criterion record was last modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: The logical comparator defining the relationship between the subject's measured value and the numeric threshold (EQ=equal, NE=not equal, LT=less than, LE=less than or equal, GT=greater than, GE=greater than or equal). Used in conjunction with numeric_threshold_value.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ISO 11179

description: The unit of measure for the numeric threshold value (e.g., years, mL/min/1.73m², kg/m², mg/dL). Follows CDISC controlled terminology for units.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ISO 11240

description: The quantitative threshold value associated with the criterion where applicable (e.g., age ≥ 18, eGFR ≥ 60, BMI ≤ 35). Used for lab value, vital sign, and demographic criteria that have a numeric boundary.
reference: CDISC SDTM IE Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The protocol version number (e.g., v1.0, v2.1) in which this criterion first became applicable. Used to determine which subjects enrolled under which protocol version were subject to this criterion.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IE Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: The protocol version number in which this criterion was last applicable before being superseded or retired. Null if the criterion is still active in the current protocol version.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IE Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether Source Data Verification (SDV) is required for this criterion during monitoring visits. When True, the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) must verify the criterion assessment against source documents at the site.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+

description: The date on which this criterion was retired or superseded. Null if the criterion remains active. Used to determine the applicable criterion set for subjects screened on a given date.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Operational guidance notes for site staff on how to assess and document this criterion during subject screening. May include clarifications, assessment methods, source document requirements, and common pitfalls. Sourced from the study's screening manual or site training materials.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM IE Domain

business_glossary_term: Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) Inclusion/Exclusion (IE) Test Code
description: CDISC SDTM-compliant short code for the criterion, conforming to the IE domain IETESTCD variable. Maximum 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters. Used for regulatory submission datasets and CDISC compliance validation.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide IE Domain; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: The type of source document required to verify this criterion (e.g., medical records, laboratory report, imaging report, physician attestation, birth certificate). Used to guide site staff and CRAs during screening and monitoring.
