description: Free-text narrative describing the circumstances of the temperature excursion, including any contextual information provided by the site, depot, or courier at the time of detection. Supports GCP audit readiness and regulatory inspection documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: Externally-known, human-readable reference number assigned to this excursion event, used in sponsor communications, QA investigations, and regulatory audit trails. Typically generated by the RTSM or CTMS system (e.g., Medidata Rave or Oracle Siebel CTMS).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone) at which the temperature excursion began — i.e., when the temperature first breached the defined threshold. This is the principal real-world event time for the excursion. Critical for duration calculation and impact assessment.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); 21 CFR Part 211.166; ALCOA+ principles

description: Current lifecycle status of the excursion event record. Drives QA workflow: open (newly detected), under_investigation (impact assessment in progress), pending_disposition (awaiting sponsor/QA decision), closed (disposition finalized), voided (false alarm or data entry error confirmed).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 211.192; MasterControl CAPA workflow

description: Classification of the excursion by the nature of the breach: high_temperature (exceeded upper limit), low_temperature (fell below lower limit), freeze_thaw (frozen product that should not be), humidity (relative humidity breach), combined (multiple parameter breach simultaneously).
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); WHO Technical Report Series No. 961 Annex 9; EU GMP Annex 13

description: The outcome of the scientific/QA impact assessment determining the usability of the affected IMP: use (product confirmed acceptable for continued use), quarantine (product held pending further evaluation), destroy (product deemed unusable and scheduled for destruction), pending (assessment not yet completed), return_to_sponsor (product to be returned to sponsor for evaluation). Critical for GCP compliance and patient safety.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ICH Q10

description: Categorizes where in the cold-chain the excursion occurred: depot (central or regional IMP warehouse), site (investigational site pharmacy or storage), in_transit (during shipment between locations), courier_hub (third-party logistics hub), customs (held at customs/border control).
reference: EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 211.142

description: The most recent calibration date of the temperature data logger at the time of the excursion. Required to validate the reliability of the recorded temperature data for GCP audit readiness and regulatory submissions.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.68; EU GMP Annex 11; ISO/IEC 17025

description: The minimum acceptable storage temperature (in degrees Celsius) defined for the affected IMP, as specified in the kit definition or product stability data. Breach of this threshold constitutes a low-temperature excursion.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.166

description: The highest temperature value (in degrees Celsius) recorded during the excursion event. Used to assess the severity of a high-temperature excursion against product stability specifications.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); USP <1079>; EU GMP Annex 13

description: The Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT) in degrees Celsius calculated for the excursion period. MKT is the single calculated temperature that, if maintained over the storage period, would produce the same thermal stress as the actual temperature fluctuations. Used per USP <1079> and WHO guidelines for stability impact assessment.
reference: USP <1079>; WHO Technical Report Series No. 961 Annex 9; ICH Q1A(R2)

description: The lowest temperature value (in degrees Celsius) recorded during the excursion event. Used to assess the severity of a low-temperature or freeze-thaw excursion against product stability specifications.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); USP <1079>; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Indicates whether replacement IMP kits need to be dispatched to the affected site or depot as a result of the disposition decision (e.g., quarantine or destroy outcome). Drives supply replenishment workflow in the RTSM (Medidata Rave).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: Name or user identifier of the person (e.g., CRC, CRA, site pharmacist, depot manager) who first reported or logged the temperature excursion into the system. Supports ALCOA+ attributability requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The date and time when the excursion was formally reported or entered into the system. May differ from excursion_start_timestamp if there was a delay in detection or reporting. Supports ALCOA+ contemporaneity assessment.
reference: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

description: High-level categorization of the root cause identified during the CAPA or investigation process: equipment_failure (refrigeration/monitoring device malfunction), process_failure (SOP not followed), human_error (incorrect handling), logistics_failure (carrier/transit failure), environmental (external weather or facility event), unknown (root cause not yet determined). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|process_failure|human_error|logistics_failure|environmental|unknown — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ISO 9001:2015; MasterControl CAPA; 21 CFR Part 820.100

description: Detailed narrative description of the identified root cause of the temperature excursion, as documented during the QA investigation. Supports CAPA development and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 211.192; ISO 9001:2015

business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) Excursion Reference
description: The excursion or alert reference identifier as recorded in the RTSM system (Medidata Rave IRT/RTSM module). Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational source system.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The date on which the sponsor was formally notified of the temperature excursion. Null if sponsor_notification_required is False or notification has not yet been sent. Used to track compliance with contractual and regulatory notification timelines.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether the sponsor must be formally notified of this excursion per the clinical supply agreement or protocol requirements. True = notification required; False = not required (e.g., minor excursion within pre-defined acceptable limits).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether the product stability data (from the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier or stability package) was formally reviewed as part of the impact assessment for this excursion. True = reviewed; False = not yet reviewed. Required for GCP compliance documentation.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13

description: The date and time when this temperature excursion record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and incremental data processing in the Databricks Lakehouse silver layer.
reference: ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The maximum acceptable storage temperature (in degrees Celsius) defined for the affected IMP, as specified in the kit definition or product stability data. Breach of this threshold constitutes a high-temperature excursion.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.166

business_glossary_term: Supply Budget Allocation - Supply Budget Allocation Id
description: Primary key for the supply_budget_allocation association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Supply Budget Allocation - Budget Line Id
description: Foreign key linking to the budget line item covered by this supply allocation
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Supply Budget Allocation - Supply Plan Id
description: Foreign key linking to the supply plan that drives this budget allocation
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Lifecycle status of this supply budget allocation record. Tracks whether the allocation is in draft, actively in use, superseded by a newer supply plan version, or closed. Required to manage versioned supply plan amendments.
reference: Structural attribute required to manage versioned allocations across supply plan amendments

description: The supply cost category (e.g., manufacturing, packaging, cold-chain distribution, destruction) that this allocation covers. Classifies which aspect of the supply plan is being mapped to this budget line.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

description: End date of the time period during which this supply plan-to-budget line allocation is active and applicable. Together with period_start_date, bounds the financial planning window for this allocation.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

description: Start date of the time period during which this supply plan-to-budget line allocation is active and applicable. Defines the temporal scope of this specific allocation record.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

description: Quantity of IMP units or supply activities allocated from this supply plan to this specific budget line. Belongs to the allocation, not to either the supply plan or budget line alone, as the same supply plan may allocate different quantities to different cost categories.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

description: Cost per unit applied to this specific supply plan-to-budget line allocation. May differ from the budget line's standard unit cost when supply plan amendments introduce revised cost assumptions for a specific allocation.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

description: Tracked variance between the planned supply cost and the actual or revised cost for this specific supply plan-to-budget line pairing. Enables clinical supply finance teams to perform variance analysis at the allocation level.
reference: Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data

business_glossary_term: Contracted Supply Item - Contracted Supply Item Id
description: Primary key for the contracted_supply_item association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Contracted Supply Item - Imp Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record that is included in this contracted supply scope.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Contracted Supply Item - Study Contract Id
description: Foreign key linking to the Clinical Trial Agreement under which this IMP supply scope is contracted.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The total quantity of this IMP agreed to be supplied under this specific contract, expressed in the IMP's dispensing unit. Belongs to the relationship because the same IMP may have different contracted quantities across different study contracts.
The date from which this IMP's supply scope becomes active and binding under the contract. May differ from the contract's own effective_start_date if the IMP is added via a change order.
The date on which this IMP's supply scope expires under the contract. May differ from the contract's effective_end_date if the IMP is removed or replaced via a change order.

The functional role this IMP plays within the study as defined in the contract scope: IMP (the investigational product under study), COMPARATOR (active reference drug), PLACEBO, RESCUE_MEDICATION, or AUXILIARY. This role is specific to the IMP-contract pairing and cannot reside on imp_master (which is study-agnostic) or study_contract (which is not IMP-specific).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Guideline — definition of IMP and auxiliary medicinal product

description: The negotiated price per dispensing unit for this IMP under this specific contract. Belongs to the relationship because the same IMP may be priced differently across different study contracts or sponsors.

business_glossary_term: Depot Sla Coverage - Depot Sla Coverage Id
description: Primary key for the depot_sla_coverage association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the clinical supply depot that is governed by the associated SLA.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Depot Sla Coverage - Service Level Agreement Id
description: Foreign key linking to the Service Level Agreement that governs the associated depot.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The date on which this SLA became binding and performance measurement began for this specific depot. Distinct from the SLA's own effective_start_date, which governs the SLA globally; this date governs when the SLA was applied to this particular depot.
reference: ISO 8601 date

description: The most recent date on which this depot-SLA assignment was formally reviewed by supply chain governance. Drives scheduling of the next review and supports audit trail requirements.
reference: ISO 8601 date

description: Current compliance state of this depot against this SLA. Reflects whether the depot is meeting, breaching, or at-risk for the SLA threshold. Belongs to the assignment, not to the depot or SLA alone.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Describes which activities, shipment types, or operational processes at this depot are covered by this SLA assignment (e.g., 'outbound IMP dispatch only', 'all temperature-controlled storage operations'). Scope may differ per depot even for the same SLA.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Primary key for the imp_authorization association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Imp Authorization - Clinical Trial Authorization Id
description: Foreign key linking to the Clinical Trial Authorization under which this IMP is authorized.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record that is authorized under this CTA.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The authorization status of this specific IMP under this specific CTA at the time of record. Distinct from the overall CTA status, as individual IMPs within a multi-IMP CTA may have different authorization states (e.g., one IMP suspended while others remain authorized).
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The quantity of the IMP authorized for use under this specific CTA, as approved by the national competent authority. Belongs to the IMP-CTA pairing, not to either entity alone, as the same IMP may have different authorized quantities under different CTAs.
reference: EU CTR 536/2014 Annex I

description: The date from which this IMP is legally authorized for use under this CTA in the specified member state. May differ from the CTA's overall effective_from_date when IMPs are added via substantial modification.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The date on which this IMP's authorization under this CTA expires or is terminated in the specified member state. Supports supply planning cutoff calculations and regulatory compliance monitoring.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: EudraCT or EudraGMDP reference number for the investigational medicinal product as registered in the EU regulatory system. Used to cross-reference IMP manufacturing and quality data with the CTA. [Moved from clinical_trial_authorization: This EudraCT/EudraGMDP reference for the IMP is a relationship-level identifier that belongs to the IMP-CTA pairing, not to the CTA alone. In a multi-IMP CTA, each IMP has its own EudraCT product number. Moving it to the association correctly models the per-IMP-per-CTA granularity.]
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; EudraGMDP; EMA

description: Name of the investigational medicinal product (IMP) covered by this Clinical Trial Authorization. Identifies the drug or biologic under investigation as declared in the CTA application dossier. [Moved from clinical_trial_authorization: This denormalized text field on clinical_trial_authorization was a workaround for the absence of a proper IMP-CTA association. With imp_authorization in place, the IMP identity is captured via the FK to imp_master, making this redundant text field unnecessary on the CTA record.]
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; EU Directive 2001/20/EC; EMA; ICH E6(R2)

description: ISO 3166-1 country code of the EU member state or non-EU jurisdiction in which this IMP is authorized under this CTA. Captures the jurisdiction-specific nature of the IMP-CTA authorization pairing.

business_glossary_term: Imp Indication Track - Imp Indication Track Id
description: Primary key for the imp_indication_track association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

business_glossary_term: Imp Indication Track - Imp Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record in the supply domain
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the therapeutic indication reference record in the program domain
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The patient selection and biomarker strategy applied to this IMP for this specific indication. The same IMP may use a biomarker-selected strategy in one indication (e.g., KRAS G12C+ NSCLC) and an all-comers strategy in another (e.g., colorectal cancer).
reference: FDA Biomarker Qualification Program; EMA Biomarker Guidance

description: The current clinical development phase for this specific IMP-indication pairing. Distinct from any aggregate phase on the IMP master or indication record — a single IMP may be in Phase III for one indication and Phase I for another simultaneously.
reference: ICH E8(R1) clinical study phase definitions

description: The intended line of therapy for this IMP in this indication (e.g., first-line, second-line). Belongs to the IMP-indication pairing — the same IMP may be studied as 1L in one indication and 2L in another.
reference: NCCN clinical practice guidelines; FDA labeling conventions

description: Current regulatory filing status (IND, CTA, NDA/BLA/MAA) for this specific IMP-indication combination. An IMP may have an active IND for one indication and a submitted NDA for another.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); EMA IMPD/CTA framework

description: Date on which development of this IMP for this indication was formally initiated (e.g., first IND filing date or first study activation date for this pairing).
Lifecycle status of this specific IMP-indication development track. Allows the business to mark individual tracks as discontinued without affecting the IMP master or indication records.

business_glossary_term: Imp Sop Applicability - Imp Sop Applicability Id
description: Primary key for the imp_sop_applicability association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the Standard Operating Procedure record in the compliance domain
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Imp Sop Applicability - Imp Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the investigational medicinal product master record in the supply domain
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The date on which this SOP version ceased to be applicable to the IMP — e.g., upon SOP retirement, supersession, or IMP discontinuation. Null if the applicability is currently active. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: GMP document control practice

description: The date on which this SOP version became formally applicable to the IMP. Typically aligned with the SOP effective_date or the IMP's first use in a study governed by this SOP. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: GCP/GMP regulatory requirement

description: The specific operational capacity in which this SOP governs the IMP — e.g., storage, dispensing, destruction, cold-chain handling. A single IMP may have multiple applicability records with different roles. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: GMP document control practice

description: Indicates whether personnel handling this specific IMP are required to complete formal training on this SOP as a condition of the IMP-SOP applicability. May differ from the SOP-level training_required flag when IMP-specific handling requirements apply. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: GCP ICH E6(R2) training requirements

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each ancillary supply record in the clinical trial supply chain. Primary key for the ancillary_supply data product.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to supply.depot. Business justification: Ancillary supplies are stored at and distributed from clinical supply depots before being shipped to investigational sites. Adding depot_id to ancillary_supply establishes the storage/sourcing depot f
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the specific protocol version that mandates the use of this ancillary supply. Ensures supply requirements are aligned with the current approved protocol amendment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; FDA 21 CFR 312.23

description: Foreign key linking to finance.purchase_order. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, eDiaries, devices, PPE) are procured via purchase orders. Finance tracks ancillary supply costs against POs for budget reconciliation and sponsor pass-through billing. Cl
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to agreement.scope_of_work. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, patient diaries, devices) are specified in the SOW as protocol-required materials with defined quantities and accountability requirements. SOW-driven ancillary supply pro
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this ancillary supply is required. Links the supply item to the protocol-defined study context.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS Study Object

description: Reference to the investigational site at which this ancillary supply stock is held or required. Enables site-level inventory tracking and reorder management.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4; Oracle Siebel CTMS Site Object

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Ancillary supplies (lab kits, patient diaries, eDiary devices) are required at specific protocol-defined visits. Linking ancillary_supply to study_visit_schedule enables visit-level supply planning an
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Current reconciliation status of the ancillary supply accountability record. Indicates whether the received, dispensed, returned, and destroyed quantities have been fully reconciled per GCP requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62; FDA Guidance on Drug Accountability

description: Current lifecycle status of the ancillary supply item at the site or study level. Drives reorder triggers, site communications, and supply chain planning actions.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country where the ancillary supply was manufactured. Required for import/export regulatory compliance and customs documentation.
reference: ISO 3166-1; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA Import Regulations

description: Timestamp when this ancillary supply record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Supply Reference
description: Reference identifier for this ancillary supply record in Oracle Siebel CTMS. Supports cross-system traceability between supply chain operations and site management activities.
reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2)

description: Current on-hand inventory quantity of the ancillary supply at the assigned site, expressed in the defined unit of measure. Updated upon receipt of shipments and dispensing events.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Medidata Rave RTSM Inventory

description: Quantity of ancillary supply that has been destroyed at the site or depot due to expiry, damage, or protocol requirements. Supports accountability reconciliation and destruction certificate documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

description: Method used to destroy expired or unused ancillary supply stock. Required for environmental compliance, regulatory inspection readiness, and accountability documentation.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62; EPA Regulations

description: Cumulative quantity of this ancillary supply dispensed to subjects or consumed in study procedures since last receipt. Used for accountability reconciliation and waste analysis.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62

description: Date from which this ancillary supply record is valid and active for the study and site. Supports protocol amendment tracking and supply version management.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date on which this ancillary supply record ceases to be valid for the study and site. Null indicates the record is currently active. Supports supply lifecycle management and study close-out.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date on which the current stock of this ancillary supply expires and must no longer be used. Critical for expiry management, destruction scheduling, and GCP compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.137

description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply requires cold-chain logistics management during storage and shipment. When true, temperature-controlled packaging and monitoring are mandatory.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); WHO Technical Report Series 961; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply is directly used by or administered to study subjects (e.g., patient diaries, injection devices). Patient-facing supplies may require additional labeling and consent documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR 164

description: Indicates whether this ancillary supply is explicitly mandated by the study protocol. Protocol-required supplies must be tracked for accountability and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; FDA 21 CFR 312.62

description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the ancillary supply label (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de-DE'). Ensures site-appropriate labeling for multi-national trials.
reference: ISO 639-1; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

description: Full text content of the label applied to the ancillary supply packaging as required by the protocol and applicable regulations. Supports label review, audit, and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.6; CDISC CDASH

description: Date on which this ancillary supply was most recently dispensed to a study subject or used in a study procedure. Supports usage tracking and expiry risk assessment.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Date of the most recent shipment of this ancillary supply to the site. Used to monitor supply chain activity, identify sites with stale stock, and support resupply planning.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; SAP S/4HANA

description: Manufacturer's lot or batch number for the current stock of ancillary supply. Essential for traceability, recall management, and ALCOA+ compliance in clinical trial accountability.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; 21 CFR 211.184; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Name of the manufacturer or supplier of the ancillary supply. Required for traceability, quality event investigations, and regulatory inspection documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ISO 14155; 21 CFR 820

description: Manufacturer's own catalogue or part number for the ancillary supply. Used for procurement ordering, quality investigations, and cross-referencing with supplier documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ISO 14155

description: Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this ancillary supply. Paired with min_storage_temp_c to define the acceptable temperature range for storage and transport.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.142

description: Upper inventory limit for this ancillary supply at the site. Prevents overstocking, reduces waste from expiry, and supports cold-chain capacity planning.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; SAP S/4HANA

description: Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this ancillary supply. Used for cold-chain monitoring, excursion detection, and GCP compliance reporting.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.142

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, handling instructions, or special requirements associated with this ancillary supply record. Supports site communications and CRA monitoring activities.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+

description: Number of individual units contained within one ordering/shipping pack of the ancillary supply. Used to convert between pack-level and unit-level inventory quantities.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Material Master; ICH E6(R2)

description: Number of days required from placement of a purchase order to receipt of the ancillary supply at the site or depot. Used for reorder planning and supply continuity risk management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ICH E6(R2)

description: Date on which the ancillary supply was received at the investigational site or depot. Used for inventory reconciliation, shelf-life calculation, and shipment confirmation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ALCOA+; 21 CFR 312.62

description: Regulatory classification of the ancillary supply under applicable medical device or in-vitro diagnostic regulations (e.g., FDA Class I/II/III device, EU MDR class). Determines labeling, CE marking, and accountability requirements.
reference: EU MDR 2017/745; 21 CFR Part 820; ISO 14155; PMDA

description: Standard quantity to be ordered when the reorder threshold is reached. Represents the economic order quantity agreed with the supplier or depot for this ancillary supply.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Procurement; ICH E6(R2)

description: Minimum stock quantity level at which a replenishment order must be triggered for this ancillary supply at the site. Supports automated reorder alerts and supply continuity planning.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Quantity of ancillary supply returned from the site to the depot or sponsor for destruction or reuse. Required for accountability reconciliation and regulatory compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 312.62

business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) Supply ID
description: Identifier assigned to this ancillary supply item within the Medidata Rave RTSM system. Enables cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational RTSM source of record.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11

description: Total shelf life of the ancillary supply in days from the date of manufacture or receipt. Used to calculate expiry dates and plan supply replenishment schedules.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Required storage condition for the ancillary supply as specified by the manufacturer or protocol (e.g., room_temperature, refrigerated). Drives cold-chain logistics and site storage compliance checks.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2); EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR 211.142

description: Broader classification grouping ancillary supplies by regulatory or operational category (e.g., medical_device, consumable, diagnostic). Determines applicable regulatory labeling and handling requirements distinct from IMP accountability rules.
reference: ISO 14155; EU MDR 2017/745; 21 CFR Part 820

description: Externally-known unique catalogue or part number assigned to this ancillary supply item by the sponsor or procurement system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA material number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and procurement ordering.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Material Master; ICH E6(R2)

description: Human-readable name of the ancillary supply item (e.g., 'Insulin Syringe 1mL', 'Sodium Chloride Diluent 0.9%', 'Patient Diary Booklet'). Used in site communications, shipment manifests, and accountability reports.
reference: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Categorical classification of the ancillary supply item indicating its functional role in the clinical trial protocol. Drives procurement, labeling, and accountability rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: syringe|diluent|infusion_set|patient_diary|lab_kit|swab|bandage|other — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; CDISC CDASH

description: Standard unit in which the ancillary supply is counted, ordered, and dispensed (e.g., 'each', 'box', 'kit', 'mL'). Used for inventory calculations, shipment manifests, and accountability reconciliation.
